There they construct an enclosure for the horse with aśvattha twigs having downward-turned points.

15.1.204.s: athāsyaite saṃbhārā upakḷptā bhavanty aśvo rūpīyo yo 'sya sadaśvānām̐ sattamas tasyānye 'parimitā niramaṇā niraṣṭāḥ kṛṣṇaś ca caturakṣo dvau dāsāv anujāyai ca putro 'nvādheyāyai ca jaratpūrvā caiṣīkaś cābhyūhaḥ saidhrakaṃ ca musalaṃ paum̐ścaleyaś ca catvāri śatāni goptṛṇām̐ śataṃ talpyānām̐ rājaputrāṇām̐ śatam arājñām ugrāṇām̐ śatam̐ sūtagrāmaṇīnām̐ śataṃ kṣattasaṃgrahītṛṇāṃ catvāro mahānta ṛtvijas
15.1.204.d: अथास्यैते संभारा उपकॢप्ता भवन्त्य् अश्वो रूपीयो यो ऽस्य सदश्वानाँ सत्तमस् तस्यान्ये ऽपरिमिता निरमणा निरष्टाः कृष्णश् च चतुरक्षो द्वौ दासाव् अनुजायै च पुत्रो ऽन्वाधेयायै च जरत्पूर्वा चैषीकश् चाभ्यूहः सैध्रकं च मुसलं पौँश्चलेयश् च चत्वारि शतानि गोप्तृणाँ शतं तल्प्यानाँ राजपुत्राणाँ शतम् अराज्ञाम् उग्राणाँ शतँ सूतग्रामणीनाँ शतं क्षत्तसंग्रहीतृणां चत्वारो महान्त ऋत्विजस्
15.1.204.m: Then for him these materials are made ready: a handsome horse that is the best of his good horses; other non-castrated, castrated [stallions] in unlimited number; a black, four-eyed [dog]; two female servants; a son by an unwed woman; a son by an inherited female slave; an old sieve, a brush of reeds, a pestle made of saidhraka wood, a son of a courtesan; four hundred guardians: a hundred princes of royal bed, a hundred noblemen not of royal blood, a hundred heralds and village chiefs, a hundred chamberlains and charioteers; the four chief officiating priests;

15.1.205.s: tān anv itare tān kāle 'padātīn samāvahanti ||
15.1.205.d: तान् अन्व् इतरे तान् काले ऽपदातीन् समावहन्ति ॥
15.1.205.m: the others following them; these they bring together at the appointed time, arriving on foot.

15.2.205.s: ā subrahmaṇyāyās | catuṣṭayīr āpo digbhyaḥ saṃbhṛtāś caturaḥ sāhasrān niṣkān suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau dve anye hiraṇye dvau vīṇāgāthinau brāhmaṇaṃ ca rājanyaṃ ca dve raśane mauñjīṃ ca kuśamayīṃ cobhe trayodaśāratnyau |
15.2.205.d: आ सुब्रह्मण्यायास् । चतुष्टयीर् आपो दिग्भ्यः संभृताश् चतुरः साहस्रान् निष्कान् सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ द्वे अन्ये हिरण्ये द्वौ वीणागाथिनौ ब्राह्मणं च राजन्यं च द्वे रशने मौञ्जीं च कुशमयीं चोभे त्रयोदशारत्न्यौ ।
15.2.205.m: Up to the Subrahmaṇyā [priest]; water of four kinds gathered from the quarters; four gold ornaments worth a thousand each; two ornaments, one of gold and one of silver; two other gold pieces; two lute-players, a brāhmaṇa and a rājanya; and two reins, one made of muñja grass and one made of kuśa grass, both thirteen cubits long.

15.2.205.s: etenopakḷptena citrām āyatīm uparamati | atha citrayā | ity araṇyor agnīn samārohya śālām abhipraiti ye te panthānaḥ savitaḥ pūrvyāso 'reṇavo vitatā antarikṣe | tebhir no adya pathibhiḥ sugebhī rakṣā ca no adhi ca deva brūhi | iti |
15.2.205.d: एतेनोपकॢप्तेन चित्राम् आयतीम् उपरमति । अथ चित्रया । इत्य् अरण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्य शालाम् अभिप्रैति ये ते पन्थानः सवितः पूर्व्यासो ऽरेणवो वितता अन्तरिक्षे । तेभिर् नो अद्य पथिभिः सुगेभी रक्षा च नो अधि च देव ब्रूहि । इति ।
15.2.205.m: With this [equipment] made ready, he waits for the Citrā [nakṣatra] to arrive; then, having mounted the fires into the kindling sticks with [the verse]: "With Citrā...", he approaches the hall with: "The paths that are thine, O Savitar, primeval, dustless, spread out in the intermediate space / by those paths, easy to traverse, do thou protect us today and bless us, O god!"

15.2.205.s: uttareṇa śālāṃ parītya pūrvayā dvārā śālāṃ prapādya gārhapatyasyāyatane mathitvāgnīn vihṛtya gārhapatyam upatiṣṭhate namo 'gnaye pṛthivikṣite lokaspṛte lokam asmai yajamānāya dehi | iti
15.2.205.d: उत्तरेण शालां परीत्य पूर्वया द्वारा शालां प्रपाद्य गार्हपत्यस्यायतने मथित्वाग्नीन् विहृत्य गार्हपत्यम् उपतिष्ठते नमो ऽग्नये पृथिविक्षिते लोकस्पृते लोकम् अस्मै यजमानाय देहि । इति
15.2.205.m: Having walked around the hall to the north, entering the hall by the eastern door, having churned [fire] in the place of the gārhapatya and having distributed the fires, he waits upon the gārhapatya with: "Homage to Agni, dwelling on the earth, space-conquering! Give space to this sacrificer!"

15.2.205.s: namo vāyave 'ntarikṣakṣite lokaspṛte lokam asmai yajamānāya dehi | ity anvāhāryapacanam |
15.2.205.d: नमो वायवे ऽन्तरिक्षक्षिते लोकस्पृते लोकम् अस्मै यजमानाय देहि । इत्य् अन्वाहार्यपचनम् ।
15.2.205.m: Upon the anvāhāryapacana with: "Homage to Vāyu, dwelling in the intermediate space, space-conquering! Give space to this sacrificer!"

15.2.206.s: namaḥ sūryāya divikṣite lokaspṛte lokam asmai yajamānāya dehi | ity āhavanīyam
15.2.206.d: नमः सूर्याय दिविक्षिते लोकस्पृते लोकम् अस्मै यजमानाय देहि । इत्य् आहवनीयम्
15.2.206.m: Upon the āhavanīya with: "Homage to Sūrya, dwelling in heaven, space-conquering! Give space to this sacrificer!"

15.2.206.s: athāsyaitat purastād eva jaghanenāśvaśālām ekāpasrāvaṃ vimitaṃ kāritaṃ bhavati
15.2.206.d: अथास्यैतत् पुरस्ताद् एव जघनेनाश्वशालाम् एकापस्रावं विमितं कारितं भवति
15.2.206.m: Then, already beforehand, behind the horse's stable, a shed with a single sloping roof has been constructed for him.

15.2.206.s: tad vṛthāgnim upasamādhāya mṛtyave svāhā mṛtyave svāhā | iti navatim āhutīr juhoti prayāsāya svāhā | ity ekādaśa
15.2.206.d: तद् वृथाग्निम् उपसमाधाय मृत्यवे स्वाहा मृत्यवे स्वाहा । इति नवतिम् आहुतीर् जुहोति प्रयासाय स्वाहा । इत्य् एकादश
15.2.206.m: Having added common fire there, he offers ninety oblations with: "To Death, hail! To Death, hail!", and eleven with: "To exertion, hail!"

15.2.206.s: śatāyur vai puruṣaḥ śatavīrya ātmaikaśato yāvān eva puruṣas tasmān mṛtyum avayajate | iti brāhmaṇam
15.2.206.d: शतायुर् वै पुरुषः शतवीर्य आत्मैकशतो यावान् एव पुरुषस् तस्मान् मृत्युम् अवयजते । इति ब्राह्मणम्
15.2.206.m: "A man has a lifespan of a hundred years, has a hundredfold strength, and his self is the hundred and first; as much as a man is, from that he drives away death by sacrificing" — thus says the brāhmaṇa passage.

15.2.206.s: atha keśaśmaśru vāpayitvā lomāni sam̐hṛtya nakhāni nikṛtya dato dhāvya snātāvahate vāsasī paridadhāte
15.2.206.d: अथ केशश्मश्रु वापयित्वा लोमानि सँहृत्य नखानि निकृत्य दतो धाव्य स्नातावहते वाससी परिदधाते
15.2.206.m: Then, having had his hair and beard shaved, his body hair clipped, his nails pared, and his teeth cleaned, having bathed, they both put on unwashed garments.
Both are adorned with human ornament and clad in unwashed garments.

15.2.206.s: athābhyāṃ vratopāyanīyaṃ pācayati tasyāśitau bhavataḥ sarpirmiśrasya payomiśrasya |
15.2.206.d: अथाभ्यां व्रतोपायनीयं पाचयति तस्याशितौ भवतः सर्पिर्मिश्रस्य पयोमिश्रस्य ।
15.2.206.m: Then he has the food for undertaking the vow cooked for them; both eat of that mixed with ghee and mixed with milk.
Then in the afternoon two pieces of gold are cast into their mouths.

15.3.206.s: suvarṇaṃ yajamāno rajataṃ patnī rajatāni vā yadi bahvyo bhavanti |
15.3.206.d: सुवर्णं यजमानो रजतं पत्नी रजतानि वा यदि बह्व्यो भवन्ति ।
15.3.206.m: A piece of gold [for] the sacrificer, a piece of silver [for] the wife, or pieces of silver if there are many [wives].

15.3.206.s: athāsya vācaṃyamasya sāyamagnihotraṃ juhoti | upasaṃgacchanta enam ete rājagṛhāḥ sūtagrāmṇyaḥ kṣattasaṃgrahītāraḥ kāruviśā iti
15.3.206.d: अथास्य वाचंयमस्य सायमग्निहोत्रं जुहोति । उपसंगच्छन्त एनम् एते राजगृहाः सूतग्राम्ण्यः क्षत्तसंग्रहीतारः कारुविशा इति
15.3.206.m: Then, while he is keeping silence, he offers the evening agnihotra; these royal household members approach him: the heralds and village chiefs, the chamberlains and charioteers, and the artisans and common folk.

15.3.206.s: tebhyaḥ paṣṭhauhīṃ vehataṃ dadāti tāṃ te pacamānā ramayanto jāgarayanta āsate |
15.3.206.d: तेभ्यः पष्ठौहीं वेहतं ददाति तां ते पचमाना रमयन्तो जागरयन्त आसते ।
15.3.206.m: To them he gives a barren cow in her fifth year; cooking it, entertaining and keeping [the sacrificer] awake, they sit [through the night].
Then in the morning, while performing the water-sipping, they snort out the two pieces of gold.

15.3.206.s: te paum̐ścaleya ādatte | athādityam udyantam upatiṣṭhante draṣṭre nama upadraṣṭre namo 'nudraṣṭre namaḥ khyātre nama upakhyātre namo 'nukhyātre namaḥ śṛṇvate nama upaśṛṇvate namo 'nuśṛṇvate namaḥ sate namo 'sate namas | jātāya namo janiṣyamāṇāya namas | bhūtāya namo bhaviṣyate namas | iti |
15.3.206.d: ते पौँश्चलेय आदत्ते । अथादित्यम् उद्यन्तम् उपतिष्ठन्ते द्रष्ट्रे नम उपद्रष्ट्रे नमो ऽनुद्रष्ट्रे नमः ख्यात्रे नम उपख्यात्रे नमो ऽनुख्यात्रे नमः शृण्वते नम उपशृण्वते नमो ऽनुशृण्वते नमः सते नमो ऽसते नमस् । जाताय नमो जनिष्यमाणाय नमस् । भूताय नमो भविष्यते नमस् । इति ।
15.3.206.m: The son of a courtesan takes them. Then they wait upon the rising sun with: "Homage to the Beholder, homage to the Overseer, homage to the Watcher! Homage to the Proclaimer, homage to the Expounder, homage to the Announcer! Homage to the Hearer, homage to the Attentive Listener, homage to the One who Listens Close! Homage to the Real, homage to the Unreal! Homage to what has been born, homage to what is to be born! Homage to what has been, homage to what will be!"

15.3.207.m: Then he portions out the sāṃgrahaṇī offering to the Viśve Devas.

15.3.207.s: sā prasiddheṣṭiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate yāvad evātrādhvaryuś ceṣṭati tāvad eṣa pratiprasthātā catuṣṭayīṣv apsu brahmaudanam̐ śrapayitvābhighāryodañcam udvāsayati |
15.3.207.d: सा प्रसिद्धेष्टिः संतिष्ठते यावद् एवात्राध्वर्युश् चेष्टति तावद् एष प्रतिप्रस्थाता चतुष्टयीष्व् अप्सु ब्रह्मौदनँ श्रपयित्वाभिघार्योदञ्चम् उद्वासयति ।
15.3.207.m: That is performed as an established sacrifice; while the adhvaryu priest is occupied with this here, the pratiprasthātṛ priest, having cooked the brahmaudana mess in the water of four kinds and poured ghee over it, removes it [from the fire] towards the north.

15.3.207.s: athaitāṃ pātrīṃ nirṇijyopastīrya tasyām etam̐ rajatam̐ rukmaṃ prakṣālitam avadadhāti
15.3.207.d: अथैतां पात्रीं निर्णिज्योपस्तीर्य तस्याम् एतँ रजतँ रुक्मं प्रक्षालितम् अवदधाति
15.3.207.m: Then, having cleansed this dish and spread [ghee] in it as an underlayer, he places into it this washed silver plate.

15.3.207.s: tasyām enam asaṃghnann ivoddharati sarpirāsecanaṃ kṛtvā prabhūtam ājyam ānīya |
15.3.207.d: तस्याम् एनम् असंघ्नन्न् इवोद्धरति सर्पिरासेचनं कृत्वा प्रभूतम् आज्यम् आनीय ।
15.3.207.m: Without breaking it apart, as it were, he lifts it out into that [vessel], making a hollow for clarified butter and pouring plentiful melted butter [into it].
Then upon [it] he places a cleansed golden ornament.

15.3.207.s: athaitān mahata ṛtvija uttarato 'nudiśam upaveśya tān anupūrvam ācamayya tebhya enaṃ bhūmim̐ spṛśann anucchindann ivopohati ||
15.3.207.d: अथैतान् महत ऋत्विज उत्तरतो ऽनुदिशम् उपवेश्य तान् अनुपूर्वम् आचमय्य तेभ्य एनं भूमिँ स्पृशन्न् अनुच्छिन्दन्न् इवोपोहति ॥
15.3.207.m: Then, having seated these principal officiating priests toward the north, according to their direction, and having made them sip water in order, he pushes this toward them, touching the ground [with it], without spilling it, as it were.

15.4.207.s: sa āha brāhmaṇāś ca rājānaś cānena māśvena medhyena svasti samāpayātā brahmajyatāyai | iti
15.4.207.d: स आह ब्राह्मणाश् च राजानश् चानेन माश्वेन मेध्येन स्वस्ति समापयाता ब्रह्मज्यतायै । इति
15.4.207.m: He says: 'O brahmins and kings, bring me safely to the end by means of this horse worthy of sacrifice, for preeminence in sacred lore!'

15.4.207.s: taṃ tathā | itītare pratyāhus | anena tvām aśvena medhyena svasti samāpayiṣyāmo brahmajyatāyai | iti |
15.4.207.d: तं तथा । इतीतरे प्रत्याहुस् । अनेन त्वाम् अश्वेन मेध्येन स्वस्ति समापयिष्यामो ब्रह्मज्यतायै । इति ।
15.4.207.m: The others answer him: 'So be it! We shall bring you safely to the end by means of this horse worthy of sacrifice, for preeminence in sacred lore.'
Then they agree upon preeminence in sacred lore for him.

15.4.208.s: athainān sam̐śāsti sakṛtsakṛt prāśyāpratyavamṛśanto dhārayādhvai | iti |
15.4.208.d: अथैनान् सँशास्ति सकृत्सकृत् प्राश्याप्रत्यवमृशन्तो धारयाध्वै । इति ।
15.4.208.m: Then he instructs them: 'Eating once each, do not touch [it] again, and hold [it].'

15.4.208.s: athaitasmin sarpirāsecane raśane saṃtarpya parikarmiṇe prayacchati
15.4.208.d: अथैतस्मिन् सर्पिरासेचने रशने संतर्प्य परिकर्मिणे प्रयच्छति
15.4.208.m: Then, having gratified the two halters in that hollow of clarified butter, he gives them to the assistant.

15.4.208.s: dvir aparaṃ prāśya praśam̐santi rāddhas te brahmaudanas | iti
15.4.208.d: द्विर् अपरं प्राश्य प्रशँसन्ति राद्धस् ते ब्रह्मौदनस् । इति
15.4.208.m: Having eaten a second portion, they praise: 'Your brahmaudana is successfully prepared!'

15.4.208.s: tebhyaś caturaḥ sāhasrān niṣkān dadāti suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau |
15.4.208.d: तेभ्यश् चतुरः साहस्रान् निष्कान् ददाति सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ ।
15.4.208.m: To them he gives four thousand gold coins, and the two ornaments, gold and silver.

15.4.208.d: अत्र ये क्षत्रस्याभिषेक्तारस् ते ऽध्वर्युम् अभिषिञ्चन्ति
15.4.208.m: Here, those who are consecrators of royal power consecrate the adhvaryu priest.

15.4.208.s: sa āha brāhmaṇāś ca rājānaś cādhvaryur etau dvau saṃvatsarau rājā bhaviṣyati tasya śuśrūṣadhvaṃ yo hāsya na śuśrūṣiṣyate sarvasvaṃ taṃ jyāsyanti | iti |
15.4.208.d: स आह ब्राह्मणाश् च राजानश् चाध्वर्युर् एतौ द्वौ संवत्सरौ राजा भविष्यति तस्य शुश्रूषध्वं यो हास्य न शुश्रूषिष्यते सर्वस्वं तं ज्यास्यन्ति । इति ।
15.4.208.m: He says: 'O brahmins and kings, the adhvaryu priest shall be king for these two years; obey him! Whoever does not obey him, of him they shall confiscate all property.'

15.4.208.s: athādhvaryur etau dvau saṃvatsarau rājā bhavati yajamāna itītaram ācakṣate
15.4.208.d: अथाध्वर्युर् एतौ द्वौ संवत्सरौ राजा भवति यजमान इतीतरम् आचक्षते
15.4.208.m: Then the adhvaryu priest is king for these two years. They designate the other as the sacrificer.

15.4.208.s: sa āha brahmann aśvaṃ medhyaṃ bhantsyāmi devebhyaḥ prajāpataye tena rādhyāsam iti
15.4.208.d: स आह ब्रह्मन्न् अश्वं मेध्यं भन्त्स्यामि देवेभ्यः प्रजापतये तेन राध्यासम् इति
15.4.208.m: He says: 'O brahman priest, I will bind the horse worthy of sacrifice for the gods, for Prajāpati; may I succeed through it!'

15.4.208.s: badhāna | itītaraḥ pratyāha devebhyaḥ prajāpataye tena rādhnuhi | iti ||
15.4.208.d: बधान । इतीतरः प्रत्याह देवेभ्यः प्रजापतये तेन राध्नुहि । इति ॥
15.4.208.m: The other answers: 'Bind it! For the gods, for Prajāpati, succeed through it!'

15.5.208.s: atha raśanām ādatte devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām ādade | iti |
15.5.208.d: अथ रशनाम् आदत्ते देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याम् आददे । इति ।
15.5.208.m: Then he takes the halter with: 'At the impulse of the divine Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take you.'

15.5.208.s: ādāyābhimantrayate | imām agṛbhṇan raśanām ṛtasya | iti
15.5.208.d: आदायाभिमन्त्रयते । इमाम् अगृभ्णन् रशनाम् ऋतस्य । इति
15.5.208.m: Having taken [it], he consecrates it with the mantra: 'They seized this halter of truth.'

15.5.208.s: tayāśvam abhidadhāti | abhidhā asi bhuvanam asi yantāsi dhartāsi so 'gniṃ vaiśvānaram̐ saprathasaṃ gaccha svāhākṛtaḥ pṛthivyāṃ yantā rāḍ yantāsi yamano dhartāsi dharuṇas | iti |
15.5.208.d: तयाश्वम् अभिदधाति । अभिधा असि भुवनम् असि यन्तासि धर्तासि सो ऽग्निं वैश्वानरँ सप्रथसं गच्छ स्वाहाकृतः पृथिव्यां यन्ता राड् यन्तासि यमनो धर्तासि धरुणस् । इति ।
15.5.208.m: With it he puts the bridle on the horse: 'You are the bridle, you are the world, you are the restrainer, you are the supporter; consecrated by svāhā, go to Agni Vaiśvānara of wide expanse!' 'On the earth, restrainer, sovereign, you are the restrainer, the governor, you are the supporter, the foundation.'
In the very same way he takes the second halter.

15.5.208.s: tayaivam evāśvam abhidadhāti te aśvasyānupṛṣṭham anupṛṇakti |
15.5.208.d: तयैवम् एवाश्वम् अभिदधाति ते अश्वस्यानुपृष्ठम् अनुपृणक्ति ।
15.5.208.m: With it he puts the bridle on the horse in the very same way. He fastens both along the back of the horse.

15.5.208.s: etasmin kāle 'nujāyai ca putro 'nvādheyāyai ca śvabandhābhyām̐ śvānam abhidhattas |
15.5.208.d: एतस्मिन् काले ऽनुजायै च पुत्रो ऽन्वाधेयायै च श्वबन्धाभ्याँ श्वानम् अभिधत्तस् ।
15.5.208.m: At this time the son of the junior wife and the son of the discarded wife put a halter on a dog with two dog-leashes.

15.5.208.s: athaiṣa paum̐ścaleyo jaratpūrvayā savyaṃ jānu veṣṭayitvā saidhrakeṇa musalena śvānam anūpatiṣṭhate |
15.5.208.d: अथैष पौँश्चलेयो जरत्पूर्वया सव्यं जानु वेष्टयित्वा सैध्रकेण मुसलेन श्वानम् अनूपतिष्ठते ।
15.5.208.m: Then this son of a harlot, having wrapped his left knee with an old garment, stands beside the dog with a pestle of saidhraka wood.

15.5.209.s: athādhvaryuḥ purastāt pratipadyate saha śatena talpyānām̐ rājaputrāṇām |
15.5.209.d: अथाध्वर्युः पुरस्तात् प्रतिपद्यते सह शतेन तल्प्यानाँ राजपुत्राणाम् ।
15.5.209.m: Then the adhvaryu priest advances in the east, together with a hundred princes eligible for the throne.

15.5.209.s: brahmā dakṣiṇataḥ saha śatenārājñām ugrāṇām | hotā paścāt saha śatena sūtagrāmaṇīnām
15.5.209.d: ब्रह्मा दक्षिणतः सह शतेनाराज्ञाम् उग्राणाम् । होता पश्चात् सह शतेन सूतग्रामणीनाम्
15.5.209.m: The brahman priest in the south, together with a hundred fierce non-royal men; the hotṛ priest in the west, together with a hundred charioteers and village headmen;
the udgātṛ priest in the north, together with a hundred chamberlains and charioteers.

15.5.209.s: madhye 'śvaḥ śvā ca | atha dakṣiṇam̐ hradam abhiprayānti dyaus te pṛṣṭham | kramair atyakramīd vājī | ākrān vājī | iti tribhir anuvākair ā kroḍād aśvam abhidhāvayanti
15.5.209.d: मध्ये ऽश्वः श्वा च । अथ दक्षिणँ ह्रदम् अभिप्रयान्ति द्यौस् ते पृष्ठम् । क्रमैर् अत्यक्रमीद् वाजी । आक्रान् वाजी । इति त्रिभिर् अनुवाकैर् आ क्रोडाद् अश्वम् अभिधावयन्ति
15.5.209.m: In the middle are the horse and the dog. Then they go forward toward a pond in the south. With the three sections [beginning with]: 'Heaven is your back', 'With strides the courser strode across', and 'The courser has neighed', they make the horse run into [the water] up to its chest.

15.5.209.s: tam adhvaryuḥ purastāt pratyaṅmukhas tiṣṭhan prokṣati | anenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyam̐ rājā vṛtraṃ vadhyāt | iti
15.5.209.d: तम् अध्वर्युः पुरस्तात् प्रत्यङ्मुखस् तिष्ठन् प्रोक्षति । अनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायँ राजा वृत्रं वध्यात् । इति
15.5.209.m: The adhvaryu priest, standing in front facing west, sprinkles it: 'Having sacrificed with this horse worthy of sacrifice, may this king slay Vṛtra!'

15.5.209.s: tasyānu prokṣaṇam̐ śataṃ talpyā rājaputrāḥ prokṣanti
15.5.209.d: तस्यानु प्रोक्षणँ शतं तल्प्या राजपुत्राः प्रोक्षन्ति
15.5.209.m: Following his sprinkling, the hundred princes eligible for the throne sprinkle [it].

15.5.209.s: brahmā dakṣiṇata udaṅmukhas tiṣṭhan prokṣati | anenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyam̐ rājāpratidhṛṣyo 'stu | iti
15.5.209.d: ब्रह्मा दक्षिणत उदङ्मुखस् तिष्ठन् प्रोक्षति । अनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायँ राजाप्रतिधृष्यो ऽस्तु । इति
15.5.209.m: The brahman priest, standing in the south facing north, sprinkles it: 'Having sacrificed with this horse worthy of sacrifice, may this king be unassailable!'

15.5.209.s: tasyānu prokṣaṇam̐ śatam arājāna ugrāḥ prokṣanti
15.5.209.d: तस्यानु प्रोक्षणँ शतम् अराजान उग्राः प्रोक्षन्ति
15.5.209.m: Following his sprinkling, the hundred fierce non-royal men sprinkle [it].

15.5.209.s: hotā paścāt prāṅmukhas tiṣṭhan prokṣati | anenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyam̐ rājāsyai viśo bahugvai bahvaśvāyai bahvajāvikāyai bahuvrīhiyavāyai bahumāṣatilāyai bahuhiraṇyāyai bahuhastikāyai bahudāsapuruṣāyai rayimatyai puṣṭimatyai bahurāyaspoṣāyai bahusarvadhanāyai rājāstu | iti
15.5.209.d: होता पश्चात् प्राङ्मुखस् तिष्ठन् प्रोक्षति । अनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायँ राजास्यै विशो बहुग्वै बह्वश्वायै बह्वजाविकायै बहुव्रीहियवायै बहुमाषतिलायै बहुहिरण्यायै बहुहस्तिकायै बहुदासपुरुषायै रयिमत्यै पुष्टिमत्यै बहुरायस्पोषायै बहुसर्वधनायै राजास्तु । इति
15.5.209.m: The hotṛ priest, standing in the west facing east, sprinkles it: 'Having sacrificed with this horse worthy of sacrifice, may this king be the king of this clan, rich in cattle, rich in horses, rich in goats and sheep, rich in rice and barley, rich in beans and sesame, rich in gold, rich in elephants, rich in male servants, possessed of wealth, possessed of prosperity, rich in increase of wealth, rich in all possessions!'
Following his sprinkling, the hundred charioteers and village headmen sprinkle [it].

15.5.209.s: udgātottarato dakṣiṇāmukhas tiṣṭhan prokṣati | anenāśvena medhyeneṣṭvāyam̐ rājā sarvam āyur etu | iti
15.5.209.d: उद्गातोत्तरतो दक्षिणामुखस् तिष्ठन् प्रोक्षति । अनेनाश्वेन मेध्येनेष्ट्वायँ राजा सर्वम् आयुर् एतु । इति
15.5.209.m: The udgātṛ priest, standing in the north facing south, sprinkles it: 'Having sacrificed with this horse worthy of sacrifice, may this king attain the full lifespan!'
Following his sprinkling, the hundred chamberlains and charioteers sprinkle [it].
'They sprinkle the horse from the quarters,' so says the brāhmaṇa passage.

15.5.209.s: athāsyaiṣa paum̐ścaleyaḥ sam̐śiṣṭoḥ bhavati yadā tvopamī vāmyatha śunaḥ praharāsi | iti |
15.5.209.d: अथास्यैष पौँश्चलेयः सँशिष्टोः भवति यदा त्वोपमी वाम्यथ शुनः प्रहरासि । इति ।
15.5.209.m: Then this son of a harlot has been instructed: 'When I wink at you, then strike the dog!'

15.5.210.s: upamīvata eṣa paum̐ścaleyaḥ saidhrakeṇa musalena śunaḥ prahanti
15.5.210.d: उपमीवत एष पौँश्चलेयः सैध्रकेण मुसलेन शुनः प्रहन्ति
15.5.210.m: As he winks, this son of a harlot strikes the dog with the pestle of saidhraka wood.
He consecrates it right from there:

15.6.210.s: yo arvantaṃ jighām̐sati tam abhyamīti varuṇas | iti
15.6.210.d: यो अर्वन्तं जिघाँसति तम् अभ्यमीति वरुणस् । इति
15.6.210.m: 'Whoever seeks to slay the courser, him Varuṇa attacks.'

15.6.210.s: tam aśvasyādhaspadam upāsya dakṣiṇāpaplāvayati paro martaḥ paraḥ śvā | iti |
15.6.210.d: तम् अश्वस्याधस्पदम् उपास्य दक्षिणापप्लावयति परो मर्तः परः श्वा । इति ।
15.6.210.m: Throwing it under the feet of the horse, he floats it away southward with: 'Away is the mortal, away the dog!'

15.6.210.s: athāsya brahmā hastaṃ gṛhṇāti brahmaṇo vā yajamānas | ahaṃ ca tvaṃ ca vṛtrahant saṃbabhūva sanibhya ā | arātīvā cid adrivo 'nu nau śūra mam̐satai bhadrā indrasya rātayas | iti |
15.6.210.d: अथास्य ब्रह्मा हस्तं गृह्णाति ब्रह्मणो वा यजमानस् । अहं च त्वं च वृत्रहन्त् संबभूव सनिभ्य आ । अरातीवा चिद् अद्रिवो ऽनु नौ शूर मँसतै भद्रा इन्द्रस्य रातयस् । इति ।
15.6.210.m: Then the brahman priest takes the sacrificer's hand, or the sacrificer takes the brahman priest's, with: 'Both I and you, O slayer of Vṛtra, have come together for gains; even the hostile one, O hero wielder of the thunderbolt, shall think of us; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.'

15.6.210.s: atraitam aiṣīkam abhyūhaṃ mauñjībhyām̐ rajjubhyām antayor abhidadhāti
15.6.210.d: अत्रैतम् ऐषीकम् अभ्यूहं मौञ्जीभ्याँ रज्जुभ्याम् अन्तयोर् अभिदधाति
15.6.210.m: Here he binds this reed-mat on both ends with two ropes of muñja grass.
To it a branch of cane is tied together.

15.6.210.s: tad etena śataṃ talpyā rājaputrā vivicyante
15.6.210.d: तद् एतेन शतं तल्प्या राजपुत्रा विविच्यन्ते
15.6.210.m: Then by means of this, the hundred princes eligible for the throne are separated.

15.6.210.s: teṣām anu vivekam itare dve anyataram antam̐ śate gṛhṇīto dve anyataram antam̐ śate
15.6.210.d: तेषाम् अनु विवेकम् इतरे द्वे अन्यतरम् अन्तँ शते गृह्णीतो द्वे अन्यतरम् अन्तँ शते
15.6.210.m: Following their separation, the others [divide]: two hundreds take one end, two hundreds take the other end.

15.6.210.s: athainān sam̐śāsti | anenaiṣīkeṇābhyūhenābhyudūhanta iva purastāt pratyañcam ūrmiṇāśvam abhidhāvayātai | iti |
15.6.210.d: अथैनान् सँशास्ति । अनेनैषीकेणाभ्यूहेनाभ्युदूहन्त इव पुरस्तात् प्रत्यञ्चम् ऊर्मिणाश्वम् अभिधावयातै । इति ।
15.6.210.m: Then he instructs them: 'Pushing water toward [it], as it were, with this reed-mat, make the horse run from east to west with a wave!'

15.6.210.s: abhidhāvyamāne 'dhvaryur yajamānaṃ vācayati | abhi kratvendra bhūr adha jman na te vivyaṅ mahimānam̐ rajām̐si | svenā hi vṛtram̐ śavasā jaghantha na śatrur antaṃ vividad yudhā te | iti |
15.6.210.d: अभिधाव्यमाने ऽध्वर्युर् यजमानं वाचयति । अभि क्रत्वेन्द्र भूर् अध ज्मन् न ते विव्यङ् महिमानँ रजाँसि । स्वेना हि वृत्रँ शवसा जघन्थ न शत्रुर् अन्तं विविदद् युधा ते । इति ।
15.6.210.m: While it is being made to run, the adhvaryu priest makes the sacrificer recite: 'Indra, you have surpassed [all] by your wisdom, then in the earth the spaces did not encompass your greatness; for by your own power you slew Vṛtra; in battle no foe found your limit.'
Then, having rolled it up, he floats it away to the south.

15.6.210.s: athaitam aśvaṃ pradakṣiṇam āvartya śālām ānayati yad vāto apo agamad indrasya tanuvaṃ priyām | etam̐ stotar etena pathā punar aśvam āvartayāsi nas | iti
15.6.210.d: अथैतम् अश्वं प्रदक्षिणम् आवर्त्य शालाम् आनयति यद् वातो अपो अगमद् इन्द्रस्य तनुवं प्रियाम् । एतँ स्तोतर् एतेन पथा पुनर् अश्वम् आवर्तयासि नस् । इति
15.6.210.m: Then, having turned this horse clockwise, he leads it to the sacrificial hall: 'Since the wind went to the waters, Indra's dear body, by this path, O chanter, make this horse turn back to us.'

15.6.211.s: tam adhvaryuḥ pūrvābhi stokīyābhir anvaiti | agnaye svāhā somāya svāhā | ity etenānuvākena punaḥpunar abhyupākāraṃ yāvad asya stokā uparamanti |
15.6.211.d: तम् अध्वर्युः पूर्वाभि स्तोकीयाभिर् अन्वैति । अग्नये स्वाहा सोमाय स्वाहा । इत्य् एतेनानुवाकेन पुनःपुनर् अभ्युपाकारं यावद् अस्य स्तोका उपरमन्ति ।
15.6.211.m: The adhvaryu priest follows it with the earlier drop-offerings, repeatedly taking up [the ladle] with this anuvāka: 'To Agni, svāhā! To Soma, svāhā!', until its drops cease.

15.6.211.s: athaitam aśvam agreṇa śālāṃ prāñcam̐ sthāpayitvā prapadyāśvasya sāvitrāṇi juhoti | agnaye svāhā vāyave svāhā | iti sapta |
15.6.211.d: अथैतम् अश्वम् अग्रेण शालां प्राञ्चँ स्थापयित्वा प्रपद्याश्वस्य सावित्राणि जुहोति । अग्नये स्वाहा वायवे स्वाहा । इति सप्त ।
15.6.211.m: Then, having stationed this horse facing east in front of the hall, he enters and offers the oblations to Savitar belonging to the horse: 'To Agni, svāhā! To Vāyu, svāhā!'—these seven.

15.6.211.s: atha sāvitram aṣṭākapālaṃ prātar nirvapati | āsādya purastād bhāgañ juhoti | agnaye svāhā svāhendrāgnibhyām iti pañca
15.6.211.d: अथ सावित्रम् अष्टाकपालं प्रातर् निर्वपति । आसाद्य पुरस्ताद् भागञ् जुहोति । अग्नये स्वाहा स्वाहेन्द्राग्निभ्याम् इति पञ्च
15.6.211.m: Then in the morning he measures out [the material for] a cake on eight potsherds to Savitar. Having placed [the oblations], he offers the previous shares: 'To Agni, svāhā!', 'To Indra-and-Agni, svāhā!'—these five.

15.6.211.s: purastāt sviṣṭakṛtastryo 'śītim aśvacaritāny upajuhoti | īṃkārāya svāheṃkṛtāya svāhā | iti |
15.6.211.d: पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतस्त्र्यो ऽशीतिम् अश्वचरितान्य् उपजुहोति । ईंकाराय स्वाहेंकृताय स्वाहा । इति ।
15.6.211.m: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, he makes the additional eighty-three offerings of the horse's movements: 'To the sound īm, svāhā! To him who has made the sound īm, svāhā!' and so on.

15.6.211.s: asamudite trayodaśa pradrāvāñ juhoti | āyanāya svāhā prāyaṇāya svāhā | iti
15.6.211.d: असमुदिते त्रयोदश प्रद्रावाञ् जुहोति । आयनाय स्वाहा प्रायणाय स्वाहा । इति
15.6.211.m: Before [the oblations are] combined, he offers the thirteen runnings: 'To approach, svāhā! To departure, svāhā!' and so on.

15.6.211.s: sā prasiddheṣṭiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | athaitam aśvaṃ pradakṣiṇam āvartya pūrvayā dvārā śālām prapādyāntarvedi prāñcam̐ sthāpayitvāha ||
15.6.211.d: सा प्रसिद्धेष्टिः संतिष्ठते । अथैतम् अश्वं प्रदक्षिणम् आवर्त्य पूर्वया द्वारा शालाम् प्रपाद्यान्तर्वेदि प्राञ्चँ स्थापयित्वाह ॥
15.6.211.m: That rite is concluded in the established manner. Then, having turned this horse clockwise, brought him into the hall through the eastern door, and stationed him facing east inside the vedi, he says:

15.7.211.s: yad vā idam āhuḥ padepade ha vā aśvasya medhyasyādhvaryur juhotīhaiva vayaṃ tad dhoṣyāmo yathā naḥ padepade hutaṃ bhaviṣyati | iti
15.7.211.d: यद् वा इदम् आहुः पदेपदे ह वा अश्वस्य मेध्यस्याध्वर्युर् जुहोतीहैव वयं तद् धोष्यामो यथा नः पदेपदे हुतं भविष्यति । इति
15.7.211.m: "Regarding what they say: 'At every step of the sacrificial horse the adhvaryu priest indeed makes an offering,' we shall make that offering right here, so that our offering will have been made at every step."

15.7.211.s: tasya patsu dhṛtīr juhoty akṣṇayā vā paryāriṇīr vā | iha dhṛtiḥ svāhā | iha vidhṛtiḥ svāhā | iha ratniḥ svāhā | iha ramatiḥ svāhā | iti |
15.7.211.d: तस्य पत्सु धृतीर् जुहोत्य् अक्ष्णया वा पर्यारिणीर् वा । इह धृतिः स्वाहा । इह विधृतिः स्वाहा । इह रत्निः स्वाहा । इह रमतिः स्वाहा । इति ।
15.7.211.m: At its feet he offers the holding-oblations, either crosswise or surrounding in turn: 'Here is stability, svāhā!', 'Here is separation, svāhā!', 'Here is joy, svāhā!', 'Here is resting, svāhā!'.

15.7.211.s: athainaṃ prāñcam utkrāmayya prokṣati prajāpataye tvā | iti purastāt | indrāgnibhyāṃ tvā | iti dakṣiṇatas | vāyave tvā | iti paścāt | viśvebhyas tvā devebhyas | ity uttaratas | devebhyas tvā | ity adhastāt sarvebhyas tvā devebhyas | ity upariṣṭāt |
15.7.211.d: अथैनं प्राञ्चम् उत्क्रामय्य प्रोक्षति प्रजापतये त्वा । इति पुरस्तात् । इन्द्राग्निभ्यां त्वा । इति दक्षिणतस् । वायवे त्वा । इति पश्चात् । विश्वेभ्यस् त्वा देवेभ्यस् । इत्य् उत्तरतस् । देवेभ्यस् त्वा । इत्य् अधस्तात् सर्वेभ्यस् त्वा देवेभ्यस् । इत्य् उपरिष्टात् ।
15.7.211.m: Then, having made it step forward toward the east, he sprinkles it: 'To Prajāpati thee!' from the front; 'To Indra-and-Agni thee!' from the south; 'To Vāyu thee!' from behind; 'To all the gods thee!' from the north; 'To the gods thee!' from below; 'To all the gods thee!' from above.

15.7.211.s: athainam atiprokṣeṇa prokṣati kṛṣyai tvā kṣemāya tvā rayyai tvā poṣāya tvā pṛthivyai tvāntarikṣāya tvā dive tvā sate tvāsate tvādbhyas tvauṣadhībhyas tvā viśvebhyas tvā bhūtebhyas | iti |
15.7.211.d: अथैनम् अतिप्रोक्षेण प्रोक्षति कृष्यै त्वा क्षेमाय त्वा रय्यै त्वा पोषाय त्वा पृथिव्यै त्वान्तरिक्षाय त्वा दिवे त्वा सते त्वासते त्वाद्भ्यस् त्वौषधीभ्यस् त्वा विश्वेभ्यस् त्वा भूतेभ्यस् । इति ।
15.7.211.m: Then he sprinkles it with the thorough sprinkling: 'To agriculture thee! To security thee! To wealth thee! To prosperity thee! To earth thee! To the intermediate space thee! To heaven thee! To the existent thee! To the non-existent thee! To the waters thee! To the plants thee! To all beings thee!'.

15.7.212.s: athāsya rūpāṇi juhoti | añjyetāya svāhā | añjisakthāya svāhā kṛṣṇāya svāhā śvetāya svāhā | ity etābhyām anuvākābhyām
15.7.212.d: अथास्य रूपाणि जुहोति । अञ्ज्येताय स्वाहा । अञ्जिसक्थाय स्वाहा कृष्णाय स्वाहा श्वेताय स्वाहा । इत्य् एताभ्याम् अनुवाकाभ्याम्
15.7.212.m: Then he offers [the oblations of] its forms: 'To the white-spotted, svāhā!', 'To the one with marked thighs, svāhā!', 'To the black, svāhā!', 'To the white, svāhā!' with these two anuvākas.

15.7.212.s: athāsyopotthāyāśvanāmabhir dakṣiṇaṃ karṇam ājapati vibhūr mātrā prabhūḥ pitrāśvo 'si hayo 'sy atyo 'si naro 'sy arvāsi saptir asi vājy asi vṛṣāsi nṛmaṇā asi yayur nāmāsi | iti |
15.7.212.d: अथास्योपोत्थायाश्वनामभिर् दक्षिणं कर्णम् आजपति विभूर् मात्रा प्रभूः पित्राश्वो ऽसि हयो ऽस्य् अत्यो ऽसि नरो ऽस्य् अर्वासि सप्तिर् असि वाज्य् असि वृषासि नृमणा असि ययुर् नामासि । इति ।
15.7.212.m: Then, standing up beside it, he whispers into its right ear with the names of the horse: 'Thou art expansive through thy mother, mighty through thy father; thou art a horse; thou art a courser; thou art a steed; thou art a hero; thou art a runner; thou art a racer; thou art a prize-winner; thou art a stallion; thou art manly-minded; yayu by name art thou.'
Then he pays homage to it: 'Follow the flight of the Ādityas!'

15.7.212.s: athainam̐ raśanābhyām utsṛjati bhūr asi bhuve tvā bhavyāya tvā bhaviṣyate tvā viśvebhyas tvā bhūtebhyas | iti |
15.7.212.d: अथैनँ रशनाभ्याम् उत्सृजति भूर् असि भुवे त्वा भव्याय त्वा भविष्यते त्वा विश्वेभ्यस् त्वा भूतेभ्यस् । इति ।
15.7.212.m: Then he releases it from the two halters: 'Thou art being; for becoming thee, for what has been thee, for what will be thee, for all beings thee!'

15.7.212.s: athainaṃ devatābhyaḥ paridadāti devā āśāpālā etaṃ devebhyo 'śvaṃ medhāya prokṣitaṃ gopāyata | iti |
15.7.212.d: अथैनं देवताभ्यः परिददाति देवा आशापाला एतं देवेभ्यो ऽश्वं मेधाय प्रोक्षितं गोपायत । इति ।
15.7.212.m: Then he entrusts it to the deities: 'O divine guardians of the quarters, guard this horse sprinkled for sacrifice for the gods!'

15.7.212.s: atrāsmā etān aparimitān niramaṇān niraṣṭān upāvasṛjanti |
15.7.212.d: अत्रास्मा एतान् अपरिमितान् निरमणान् निरष्टान् उपावसृजन्ति ।
15.7.212.m: Thereupon they set loose towards it these uncounted geldings, castrated ones.

15.7.212.s: atrainam etāni catvāri śatāni goptṛṇām anuyuñjate prāstakavacā vitatavarūthā yathā yuddhāya tathā
15.7.212.d: अत्रैनम् एतानि चत्वारि शतानि गोप्तृणाम् अनुयुञ्जते प्रास्तकवचा विततवरूथा यथा युद्धाय तथा
15.7.212.m: Thereupon they assign these four hundred guardians to follow it, with coats of mail put on and shields unfolded, as if for battle.
He authorizes the cooked meal for them.

15.8.212.s: sa āha brāhmaṇāś ca rājānaś ca yasyeme pakvāśanam upāvahariṣyante mayāprasūtā mopavādiṣṭa | iti
15.8.212.d: स आह ब्राह्मणाश् च राजानश् च यस्येमे पक्वाशनम् उपावहरिष्यन्ते मयाप्रसूता मोपवादिष्ट । इति
15.8.212.m: He says: "O brāhmaṇas and kings, to whomsoever among you these [guardians] bring cooked food, do not speak ill [of it], authorized by me."

15.8.212.s: sa āha brāhmaṇāś ca rājānaś ca bahir devayajanād vāhanaṃ vyudacadhvaṃ yasyāyaṃ vaḍabādhiḥ sam̐sṛjyate sarvasvaṃ taṃ jyāsyanti | iti
15.8.212.d: स आह ब्राह्मणाश् च राजानश् च बहिर् देवयजनाद् वाहनं व्युदचध्वं यस्यायं वडबाधिः सँसृज्यते सर्वस्वं तं ज्यास्यन्ति । इति
15.8.212.m: He says: "O brāhmaṇas and kings, drive away your mounts outside the sacrificial ground; to whomsoever this [horse] comes into contact because of a mare, they will deprive him of all his possessions."
They drive their mounts outside the sacrificial ground.

15.8.212.s: aśvaiś caiva sāṇḍaiś caranty aśvataraiś ca na vaḍabābhir nāśvatarībhis |
15.8.212.d: अश्वैश् चैव साण्डैश् चरन्त्य् अश्वतरैश् च न वडबाभिर् नाश्वतरीभिस् ।
15.8.212.m: And they move only with uncastrated horses and with mules, not with mares, nor with she-mules.

15.8.213.s: athaitau vīṇāgāthināv atipragṛhṇītas | athaiṣa brāhmaṇo vīṇāgāthī gāyati | ity adadās | ity ayajathās | ity apacathās | ity evaṃ miśrās tisro gāthās |
15.8.213.d: अथैतौ वीणागाथिनाव् अतिप्रगृह्णीतस् । अथैष ब्राह्मणो वीणागाथी गायति । इत्य् अददास् । इत्य् अयजथास् । इत्य् अपचथास् । इत्य् एवं मिश्रास् तिस्रो गाथास् ।
15.8.213.m: Then these two lute-playing bards take up [their songs]. Then this brāhmaṇa lute-playing bard sings: 'Thus thou gavest', 'Thus thou sacrificedst', 'Thus thou cookedst'—these three mixed songs.

15.8.213.s: kāmacāro 'śvasya snānāc caivainaṃ gopāyanti vāhanāc ca |
15.8.213.d: कामचारो ऽश्वस्य स्नानाच् चैवैनं गोपायन्ति वाहनाच् च ।
15.8.213.m: The horse wanders at will. They guard it from bathing and from being ridden.

15.8.213.s: atha yady aśvam upatapad vindaty āgneyo 'ṣṭākapālaḥ saumyaś caruḥ sāvitro 'ṣṭākapālaḥ pauṣṇaś carū raudraś carur iti |
15.8.213.d: अथ यद्य् अश्वम् उपतपद् विन्दत्य् आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालः सौम्यश् चरुः सावित्रो ऽष्टाकपालः पौष्णश् चरू रौद्रश् चरुर् इति ।
15.8.213.m: Now, if an illness befalls the horse, there is a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, a caru to Soma, a cake on eight potsherds to Savitar, a caru to Pūṣan, and a caru to Rudra.

15.8.213.s: atha yadi nāv agacchaty agnaye vaiśvānarāya dvādaśakapālo mṛgākhara iti |
15.8.213.d: अथ यदि नाव् अगच्छत्य् अग्नये वैश्वानराय द्वादशकपालो मृगाखर इति ।
15.8.213.m: Then, if it reaches a boat, there is a cake on twelve potsherds to Agni Vaiśvānara at a deer-mound.

15.8.213.s: atha yadi vaḍabādhiḥ sam̐sṛjyate 'gnaye 'm̐homuce 'ṣṭākapālaḥ sauryaṃ payo vāyavya ājyabhāgas |
15.8.213.d: अथ यदि वडबाधिः सँसृज्यते ऽग्नये ऽँहोमुचे ऽष्टाकपालः सौर्यं पयो वायव्य आज्यभागस् ।
15.8.213.m: Then, if it comes into contact [with a mare] because of a mare, there is a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Aṃhomuc, milk to Sūrya, and a portion of clarified butter to Vāyu.

15.8.213.s: yadi srāvaḥ pauṣṇas | yady apsu vāruṇas | yadi kāṇaḥ sauryas |
15.8.213.d: यदि स्रावः पौष्णस् । यद्य् अप्सु वारुणस् । यदि काणः सौर्यस् ।
15.8.213.m: If there is a discharge, [an oblation] to Pūṣan; if into the water, to Varuṇa; if it becomes blind in one eye, to Sūrya.

15.8.213.s: etāsām ārtīnāṃ yāṃ kāṃ ca nyeti sakṛt tv eva prāyaścittis | atha yo 'sya sadaśvānām̐ sattamas tam utsṛjati |
15.8.213.d: एतासाम् आर्तीनां यां कां च न्येति सकृत् त्व् एव प्रायश्चित्तिस् । अथ यो ऽस्य सदश्वानाँ सत्तमस् तम् उत्सृजति ।
15.8.213.m: Whichever of these misfortunes it falls into, the expiation is made only once. Then he releases that one of his good horses which is the best.
Now from that point he proceeds with the two halters indeed.
The procedure is identical up to the entrustment.

15.9.213.s: utsṛjyāśvaṃ vaiśvadevān paśūn ālabhante teṣāṃ paśupuroḍāśān anuvartante vaiśvadevahavīm̐ṣi
15.9.213.d: उत्सृज्याश्वं वैश्वदेवान् पशून् आलभन्ते तेषां पशुपुरोडाशान् अनुवर्तन्ते वैश्वदेवहवीँषि
15.9.213.m:
Having released the horse, they seize the animal victims for the Viśvedevas. The Vaiśvadeva oblations follow after their animal cakes.

Or rather, the Vaiśvadeva oblations become their animal cakes.

15.9.213.s: tān anuvartate madhyamā sāvitrī prasiddhāḥ paśavaḥ saṃtiṣṭhante |
15.9.213.d: तान् अनुवर्तते मध्यमा सावित्री प्रसिद्धाः पशवः संतिष्ठन्ते ।
15.9.213.m: The middle [offering] to Savitar follows them. The animal sacrifice is concluded in the established manner.

15.9.214.s: athāparāhṇe savitra āsavitre puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
15.9.214.d: अथापराह्णे सवित्र आसवित्रे पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति
15.9.214.m: Then in the afternoon he measures out a cake on twelve potsherds to Savitar Āsavitar.

15.9.214.s: sā prasiddheṣṭiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvā prasiddhaṃ nivartayate |
15.9.214.d: सा प्रसिद्धेष्टिः संतिष्ठते । अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वा प्रसिद्धं निवर्तयते ।
15.9.214.m: That rite is concluded in the established manner. Then, having offered the full-moon rite and the Vaimṛdha rite, he turns back in the established manner.
Then these two lute-playing bards take up [their songs].

15.9.214.s: athaiṣa rājanyo vīṇāgāthī gāyati | ity ajinās | ity ayudhyathās | ity amum̐ saṃgrāmam ahan | ity evaṃ miśrās tisro gāthāḥ
15.9.214.d: अथैष राजन्यो वीणागाथी गायति । इत्य् अजिनास् । इत्य् अयुध्यथास् । इत्य् अमुँ संग्रामम् अहन् । इत्य् एवं मिश्रास् तिस्रो गाथाः
15.9.214.m: Then this noble lute-playing bard sings: 'Thus thou conqueredst', 'Thus thou foughtest', 'Thus thou didst win that battle'—these three mixed songs.

15.9.214.s: prātaragnihotre hute brāhmaṇo vīṇāgāthī gāyati sāyamagnihotre hute rājanyas
15.9.214.d: प्रातरग्निहोत्रे हुते ब्राह्मणो वीणागाथी गायति सायमग्निहोत्रे हुते राजन्यस्
15.9.214.m: When the morning agnihotra has been offered, the brāhmaṇa lute-playing bard sings; when the evening agnihotra has been offered, the noble [bard sings].

15.9.214.s: tāv evam eva saṃvatsaraṃ gāyatas | atha sāvitram aṣṭākapālaṃ prātar nirvapati |
15.9.214.d: ताव् एवम् एव संवत्सरं गायतस् । अथ सावित्रम् अष्टाकपालं प्रातर् निर्वपति ।
15.9.214.m: The two sing in this very way for a year. Then in the morning he measures out [the oblation] on eight potsherds to Savitar.

15.9.214.s: āsādya purastād bhāgāñ juhoti | asamudite dhṛtīś ca juhoti pradrāvām̐ś ca juhoti
15.9.214.d: आसाद्य पुरस्ताद् भागाञ् जुहोति । असमुदिते धृतीश् च जुहोति प्रद्रावाँश् च जुहोति
15.9.214.m: Having placed [the oblations], he offers the previous shares. Before [the oblations are] combined, he offers the holding-oblations and offers the runnings.
That rite is concluded in the established manner.

15.9.214.s: atha madhyaṃdine savitre prasavitre puroḍāśam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
15.9.214.d: अथ मध्यंदिने सवित्रे प्रसवित्रे पुरोडाशम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपति
15.9.214.m: Then at midday he measures out a cake on eleven potsherds to Savitar Prasavitar.

15.9.214.s: sā prasiddheṣṭiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | athāparāhṇe savitra āsavitre dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
15.9.214.d: सा प्रसिद्धेष्टिः संतिष्ठते । अथापराह्णे सवित्र आसवित्रे द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति
15.9.214.m: That rite is concluded in the established manner. Then in the afternoon he measures out [a cake] on twelve potsherds to Savitar Āsavitar.
That rite is concluded in the established manner.

15.9.214.s: atha śvo bhūte sāvitrībhir eva pratipadyate sa evam eva sāvitrībhir aharahar yajamānaś caturo māsa eti kāmam iṣṭyā kāmaṃ paśubandhena kāmaṃ yavāgrayaṇena |
15.9.214.d: अथ श्वो भूते सावित्रीभिर् एव प्रतिपद्यते स एवम् एव सावित्रीभिर् अहरहर् यजमानश् चतुरो मास एति कामम् इष्ट्या कामं पशुबन्धेन कामं यवाग्रयणेन ।
15.9.214.m: Then on the next day he proceeds with the [offerings] to Savitar indeed. Thus, the sacrificer, offering daily with the [rites] to Savitar, proceeds for four months, optionally with an iṣṭi, optionally with an animal sacrifice, optionally with the first-fruits of barley.

15.9.214.s: atha caturṣu māseṣu paryaveteṣu sāvitryeṣṭyeṣṭvā varuṇapraghāsān paśūn ālabhante ||
15.9.214.d: अथ चतुर्षु मासेषु पर्यवेतेषु सावित्र्येष्ट्येष्ट्वा वरुणप्रघासान् पशून् आलभन्ते ॥
15.9.214.m: Then, when four months have passed, having offered the offering to Savitar, they seize the animal victims for the Varuṇapraghāsa.

15.10.214.s: teṣāṃ paśupuroḍāśān anuvartante varuṇapraghāsahavīm̐ṣi varuṇapraghāsahavīm̐ṣi vaivaiṣāṃ paśupuroḍāśā bhavanti
15.10.214.d: तेषां पशुपुरोडाशान् अनुवर्तन्ते वरुणप्रघासहवीँषि वरुणप्रघासहवीँषि वैवैषां पशुपुरोडाशा भवन्ति
15.10.214.m: The Varuṇapraghāsa oblations follow after their animal cakes, or rather the Varuṇapraghāsa oblations become their animal cakes.
The middle [offering] to Savitar follows them.

15.10.214.s: prasiddhāḥ paśavaḥ saṃtiṣṭhante | athāparāhṇe savitra āsavitre puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
15.10.214.d: प्रसिद्धाः पशवः संतिष्ठन्ते । अथापराह्णे सवित्र आसवित्रे पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति
15.10.214.m: The animal sacrifices are concluded in the established manner. Then in the afternoon, he pours out [the material for] a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitar Āsavitra.

15.10.215.m: That offering is concluded in the established manner.
Then, having offered the full moon offering and the Vaimṛdha offering, he causes [his hair] to be shaved in the established manner.

15.10.215.s: atha śvo bhūte sāvitrībhir eva pratipadyate sa evam eva sāvitrībhir aharahar yajamāno 'parām̐ś caturo māsa eti kāmam iṣṭyā kāmaṃ paśubandhena kāmam̐ śyāmākāgrayaṇena |
15.10.215.d: अथ श्वो भूते सावित्रीभिर् एव प्रतिपद्यते स एवम् एव सावित्रीभिर् अहरहर् यजमानो ऽपराँश् चतुरो मास एति कामम् इष्ट्या कामं पशुबन्धेन कामँ श्यामाकाग्रयणेन ।
15.10.215.m: Then on the next day, he begins with the Sāvitra [offerings] alone. Sacrificing thus with the Sāvitra [offerings] day after day, he spends the next four months, according to his wish with an offering, according to his wish with an animal sacrifice, according to his wish with the first-fruits offering of wild rice (śyāmāka).

15.10.215.s: atha caturṣu māseṣu paryaveteṣu paurṇamāsyā upavasatha ānīkavataṃ paśum ālabhate
15.10.215.d: अथ चतुर्षु मासेषु पर्यवेतेषु पौर्णमास्या उपवसथ आनीकवतं पशुम् आलभते
15.10.215.m: Then, when the four months have elapsed, on the fast-day of the full moon he seizes an animal for Agni Anīkavat.
The oblation to Agni Anīkavat follows its animal-cake;

15.10.215.s: ānīkavato vaivāsya paśupuroḍāśo bhavati tam anuvartate prathamā sāvitrī
15.10.215.d: आनीकवतो वैवास्य पशुपुरोडाशो भवति तम् अनुवर्तते प्रथमा सावित्री
15.10.215.m: or rather, the oblation to Agni Anīkavat becomes its animal-cake. The first Sāvitra [offering] follows it.

15.10.215.s: prasiddhaḥ paśuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | atha madhyaṃdine saṃtapanaṃ paśum ālabhate
15.10.215.d: प्रसिद्धः पशुः संतिष्ठते । अथ मध्यंदिने संतपनं पशुम् आलभते
15.10.215.m: The animal sacrifice is concluded in the established manner. Then at midday, he seizes an animal for the Maruts Saṃtapana.
The oblation to the Maruts Saṃtapana follows its animal-cake;

15.10.215.s: saṃtapano vaivāsya paśupuroḍāśo bhavati tam anuvartate madhyamā sāvitrī
15.10.215.d: संतपनो वैवास्य पशुपुरोडाशो भवति तम् अनुवर्तते मध्यमा सावित्री
15.10.215.m: or rather, the oblation to the Maruts Saṃtapana becomes its animal-cake. The middle Sāvitra [offering] follows it.

15.10.215.s: prasiddhaḥ paśuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | athāparāhṇe savitra āsavitre puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
15.10.215.d: प्रसिद्धः पशुः संतिष्ठते । अथापराह्णे सवित्र आसवित्रे पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति
15.10.215.m: The animal sacrifice is concluded in the established manner. Then in the afternoon, he pours out [the material for] a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitar Āsavitra.
That offering is concluded in the established manner.

15.10.215.s: atha sāyaṃ gṛhamedhīyena carati | athāpararātre pūrṇadarvyeṇa carati |
15.10.215.d: अथ सायं गृहमेधीयेन चरति । अथापररात्रे पूर्णदर्व्येण चरति ।
15.10.215.m: Then in the evening he proceeds with the Gṛhamedhīya. Then in the latter part of the night he proceeds with the Pūrṇadarvya.
Then in the morning [there is] the oblation to the Maruts Krīḍin;
or rather, the oblation to the Maruts Krīḍin becomes its animal-cake.

15.10.215.s: tam anuvartate prathamā sāvitrī prasiddhaḥ paśuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | atha madhyaṃdine sākamedhān paśūn ālabhante ||
15.10.215.d: तम् अनुवर्तते प्रथमा सावित्री प्रसिद्धः पशुः संतिष्ठते । अथ मध्यंदिने साकमेधान् पशून् आलभन्ते ॥
15.10.215.m: The first Sāvitra [offering] follows it. The animal sacrifice is concluded in the established manner. Then at midday, they seize the Sākamedha animals.

15.11.216.s: teṣāṃ paśupuroḍāśān anuvartante mahāhavīm̐ṣi mahāhavīm̐ṣi vaivaiṣāṃ paśupuroḍāśā bhavanti
15.11.216.d: तेषां पशुपुरोडाशान् अनुवर्तन्ते महाहवीँषि महाहवीँषि वैवैषां पशुपुरोडाशा भवन्ति
15.11.216.m: The Mahāhavis oblations follow their animal-cakes; or rather, the Mahāhavis oblations become their animal-cakes.

15.11.216.s: prasiddhāḥ paśavaḥ saṃtiṣṭhante | athāparāhṇe pitṛyajñena carati
15.11.216.d: प्रसिद्धाः पशवः संतिष्ठन्ते । अथापराह्णे पितृयज्ञेन चरति
15.11.216.m: The animal sacrifices are concluded in the established manner. Then in the afternoon he proceeds with the ancestral sacrifice (pitṛyajña).

15.11.216.s: pitṛyajñena caritvā traiyambakaiś carati traiyambakaiś caritvādityaṃ paśum ālabhate
15.11.216.d: पितृयज्ञेन चरित्वा त्रैयम्बकैश् चरति त्रैयम्बकैश् चरित्वादित्यं पशुम् आलभते
15.11.216.m: Having proceeded with the ancestral sacrifice, he proceeds with the Traiyambaka [offerings]. Having proceeded with the Traiyambaka [offerings], he seizes an animal for Aditi.
The oblation to Aditi follows its animal-cake;

15.11.216.s: ādityo vaivāsya paśupuroḍāśo bhavati tam anuvartata uttamā sāvitrī
15.11.216.d: आदित्यो वैवास्य पशुपुरोडाशो भवति तम् अनुवर्तत उत्तमा सावित्री
15.11.216.m: or rather, the oblation to Aditi becomes its animal-cake. The last Sāvitra [offering] follows it.

15.11.216.s: prasiddhaḥ paśuḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvā prasiddhaṃ nivartayate |
15.11.216.d: प्रसिद्धः पशुः संतिष्ठते । अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वा प्रसिद्धं निवर्तयते ।
15.11.216.m: The animal sacrifice is concluded in the established manner. Then, having offered the full moon offering and the Vaimṛdha offering, he causes [his hair] to be shaved in the established manner.

15.11.216.s: atha śvo bhūte sāvitrībhir eva pratipadyate
15.11.216.d: अथ श्वो भूते सावित्रीभिर् एव प्रतिपद्यते
15.11.216.m: Then on the next day, he begins with the Sāvitra [offerings] alone.

15.11.216.s: sa evam eva sāvitrībhir aharahar yajamāno 'rdhacaturthān māsa eti kāmam iṣṭyā kāmaṃ paśubandhena kāmaṃ vrīhyāgrayaṇena |
15.11.216.d: स एवम् एव सावित्रीभिर् अहरहर् यजमानो ऽर्धचतुर्थान् मास एति कामम् इष्ट्या कामं पशुबन्धेन कामं व्रीह्याग्रयणेन ।
15.11.216.m: Sacrificing thus with the Sāvitra [offerings] day after day, he spends three and a half months, according to his wish with an offering, according to his wish with an animal sacrifice, according to his wish with the first-fruits offering of rice (vrīhi).

15.11.216.s: athāmāvāsyāyā upavasathīye 'han sāvitryeṣṭyeṣṭvāgnikāni sāvitrāṇi hutvokhāḥ saṃbhṛtya paśuśīrṣāṇi ca vāyavyaṃ paśum ālabhate
15.11.216.d: अथामावास्याया उपवसथीये ऽहन् सावित्र्येष्ट्येष्ट्वाग्निकानि सावित्राणि हुत्वोखाः संभृत्य पशुशीर्षाणि च वायव्यं पशुम् आलभते
15.11.216.m: Then on the fast-day of the new moon, having offered with the Sāvitra offering, having made the Sāvitra offerings connected with the fire, having collected the fire-pans and the animal heads, he seizes an animal for Vāyu.

15.11.216.s: tasya prājāpatyas tūpara upālambhyo bhavati tayoḥ prasiddhaṃ vapābhyāṃ caritvā paśupuroḍāśau nirvapati
15.11.216.d: तस्य प्राजापत्यस् तूपर उपालम्भ्यो भवति तयोः प्रसिद्धं वपाभ्यां चरित्वा पशुपुरोडाशौ निर्वपति
15.11.216.m: A hornless [goat] for Prajāpati is to be seized along with it. Having proceeded with the omenta of both in the established manner, he pours out [the material for] two animal-cakes.

15.11.216.s: prasiddhau paśū saṃtiṣṭhete athāparāhṇe savitra āsavitre puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
15.11.216.d: प्रसिद्धौ पशू संतिष्ठेते अथापराह्णे सवित्र आसवित्रे पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति
15.11.216.m: The two animal sacrifices are concluded in the established manner. Then in the afternoon, he pours out [the material for] a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitar Āsavitra.
That offering is concluded in the established manner.

15.11.216.s: atha śvo bhūte sāvitrībhir eva pratipadyate sa evam eva sāvitrībhir aharahar yajamāna etam ardhamāsam eti kāmam iṣṭyā kāmaṃ paśubandhena |
15.11.216.d: अथ श्वो भूते सावित्रीभिर् एव प्रतिपद्यते स एवम् एव सावित्रीभिर् अहरहर् यजमान एतम् अर्धमासम् एति कामम् इष्ट्या कामं पशुबन्धेन ।
15.11.216.m: Then on the next day, he begins with the Sāvitra [offerings] alone. Sacrificing thus with the Sāvitra [offerings] day after day, he spends this half-month, according to his wish with an offering, according to his wish with an animal sacrifice.
Then, when the four months have elapsed, having offered with the Sāvitra offering,

15.12.216.s: śunāsīrīyān paśūn ālabhante teṣāṃ paśupuroḍāśān anuvartante śunāsīrīyahavīm̐ṣi
15.12.216.d: शुनासीरीयान् पशून् आलभन्ते तेषां पशुपुरोडाशान् अनुवर्तन्ते शुनासीरीयहवीँषि
15.12.216.m:
they seize the Śunāsīrīya animals. The Śunāsīrīya oblations follow their animal-cakes;

or rather, the Śunāsīrīya oblations become their animal-cakes.

15.12.217.s: tān anuvartate madhyamā sāvitrī prasiddhāḥ paśavaḥ saṃtiṣṭhante |
15.12.217.d: तान् अनुवर्तते मध्यमा सावित्री प्रसिद्धाः पशवः संतिष्ठन्ते ।
15.12.217.m: The middle Sāvitra [offering] follows them. The animal sacrifices are concluded in the established manner.

15.12.217.s: athāparāhṇe savitra āsavitre puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
15.12.217.d: अथापराह्णे सवित्र आसवित्रे पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति
15.12.217.m: Then in the afternoon, he pours out [the material for] a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitar Āsavitra.

15.12.217.s: sā prsiddheṣṭiḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | atha paurṇamāsavaimṛdhābhyām iṣṭvā yajamānāyatana upaviśya treṇyā śalalyā lohitāyasasya ca kṣureṇa śīrṣan ni ca vartayate pari ca vapate purastād evāgre 'tha dakṣiṇato 'tha paścād athottarato 'thopariṣṭāt
15.12.217.d: सा प्र्सिद्धेष्टिः संतिष्ठते । अथ पौर्णमासवैमृधाभ्याम् इष्ट्वा यजमानायतन उपविश्य त्रेण्या शलल्या लोहितायसस्य च क्षुरेण शीर्षन् नि च वर्तयते परि च वपते पुरस्ताद् एवाग्रे ऽथ दक्षिणतो ऽथ पश्चाद् अथोत्तरतो ऽथोपरिष्टात्
15.12.217.m: That offering is concluded in the established manner. Then, having offered the full moon offering and the Vaimṛdha offering, having sat down in the sacrificer's place, he has his hair cut and shaved around on his head with a porcupine quill with three white spots and a copper razor—first on the east, then on the south, then on the west, then on the north, then on top.
The seasonal animal sacrifices are concluded; the Sāvitra [offerings] are concluded.

15.13.217.s: athāśvaśālāyām aśvaṃ nigrathnanti | athainaṃ tīrthād ānīya pavayitvā trihaviṣam agnidīkṣaṇīyām iṣṭiṃ nirvapati
15.13.217.d: अथाश्वशालायाम् अश्वं निग्रथ्नन्ति । अथैनं तीर्थाद् आनीय पवयित्वा त्रिहविषम् अग्निदीक्षणीयाम् इष्टिं निर्वपति
15.13.217.m: Then they tie up the horse in the horse-stall. Then having brought him from the watering-place and purified him, he pours out the consecration offering for the fire (agnidīkṣaṇīyā iṣṭi) with three oblations.
As many rites are omitted from it as are omitted from the [regular] consecration offering (dīkṣaṇīyā).

15.13.217.s: athādhvaryuḥ pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya pratyaṅṅ ādrutya patnīḥ saṃyājya prāṅ ety dhruvām āpyāyya trīṇi pūrvāṇi vaiśvadevāni juhoti svāhādhim ādhītāya svāhā | iti |
15.13.217.d: अथाध्वर्युः प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य प्रत्यङ्ङ् आद्रुत्य पत्नीः संयाज्य प्राङ् एत्य् ध्रुवाम् आप्याय्य त्रीणि पूर्वाणि वैश्वदेवानि जुहोति स्वाहाधिम् आधीताय स्वाहा । इति ।
15.13.217.m: Then the adhvaryu priest, having turned clockwise, having run towards the west, having performed the offerings with the wives, having gone towards the east, having swelled the dhruvā spoon, makes three former Vaiśvadeva oblations with: 'To Adhi, to the pondered, svāhā!'

15.13.217.s: atha sapta prāṇāhutīr juhoti prāṇāya svāhā vyānāya svāhā | iti |
15.13.217.d: अथ सप्त प्राणाहुतीर् जुहोति प्राणाय स्वाहा व्यानाय स्वाहा । इति ।
15.13.217.m: Then he offers seven vital-breath libations with: 'To prāṇa, svāhā! To vyāna, svāhā!'

15.13.217.s: ekavim̐śinīṃ dīkṣāṃ juhoti pṛthivyai svāhāntarikṣāya svāhā | iti
15.13.217.d: एकविँशिनीं दीक्षां जुहोति पृथिव्यै स्वाहान्तरिक्षाय स्वाहा । इति
15.13.217.m: He offers the twenty-one-part consecration libation with: 'To the earth, svāhā! To the intermediate space, svāhā!'

15.13.217.s: pañcādhvaradīkṣāhutīr juhoti ṣaḍ agnidīkṣā ekām ṛtudīkṣāṃ bhuvo devānāṃ karmaṇā | iti
15.13.217.d: पञ्चाध्वरदीक्षाहुतीर् जुहोति षड् अग्निदीक्षा एकाम् ऋतुदीक्षां भुवो देवानां कर्मणा । इति
15.13.217.m: He offers five consecration libations for the rite: 'Six fire consecrations, one season consecration, with the work of the gods, bhuvaḥ!'

15.13.217.s: saptāhāny etayeṣṭyā yajata iti sa trīṇitrīṇy eva pūrvāṇi vaiśvadevāni juhoty uttarāmuttarām ṛtudīkṣām |
15.13.217.d: सप्ताहान्य् एतयेष्ट्या यजत इति स त्रीणित्रीण्य् एव पूर्वाणि वैश्वदेवानि जुहोत्य् उत्तरामुत्तराम् ऋतुदीक्षाम् ।
15.13.217.m: 'He sacrifices for seven days with this offering'—thus [it is said]. He offers three former Vaiśvadeva [libations] each time, and an ever-later season consecration libation.

15.13.217.s: dve antata ṛtudīkṣe juhoti mahīm ū ṣu sutrāmāṇam iti | etad evāhar dīkṣate
15.13.217.d: द्वे अन्तत ऋतुदीक्षे जुहोति महीम् ऊ षु सुत्रामाणम् इति । एतद् एवाहर् दीक्षते
15.13.217.m: At the end he offers two season consecration libations with: 'May the great [goddesses] well...' [and] 'Of good protection...'. On this very day he undergoes consecration.

15.13.218.s: saṃvatsaram ukhyaṃ bibharti dvādaśopasadas | atrainam etā yathāmnātaṃ viśaḥ paryavasyanti
15.13.218.d: संवत्सरम् उख्यं बिभर्ति द्वादशोपसदस् । अत्रैनम् एता यथाम्नातं विशः पर्यवस्यन्ति
15.13.218.m: He carries the pan-fire (ukhya) for a year. There are twelve upasads. At this time these subjects settle around him as handed down by tradition.

15.13.218.s: nedīya enam ete karmakṛta upasaṃgacchante takṣāṇaś ca rathakṛtaś ca mayaskṛtaś ca kulālāś ca dvayāḥ karmārā nakhakṛtaḥ saptame |
15.13.218.d: नेदीय एनम् एते कर्मकृत उपसंगच्छन्ते तक्षाणश् च रथकृतश् च मयस्कृतश् च कुलालाश् च द्वयाः कर्मारा नखकृतः सप्तमे ।
15.13.218.m: These workmen approach him closer: carpenters, chariot-makers, leather-workers, potters, two kinds of smiths, and barbers as the seventh.

15.14.218.s: ekaśataṃ bailvāni dārvācitāni chindata tāni pravakalāni kṛtvācāya cinutaikavim̐śatiṃ yūpāñ chindataikavim̐śaty aratnīn rājjudālam agniṣṭhaṃ pautudravāv upasthāvānau ṣaḍ bailvān ṣaṭ khādirān ṣaṭ pālāśān pālāśam upaśayaṃ pālāśaṃ pātnīvataṃ pālāśaṃ viśālayūpam ekatayāni dārumayāṇi pātrāṇi kuruta ṣaṭtrim̐śatam̐ sruvān dīrghadaṇḍān ṣaṭtrim̐śatam anuveṣān dīrghadaṇḍām̐ś catvāri vāṣṭau vendrāṇasāni catuś cakrāṇi bṛhaccakrāṇi yathā samāni yūpāgraiḥ syur aparimitāny ārohaṇamahānasāni kurutaikaṃ vaitasaṃ kaṭaṃ kurutāśvasyopastaraṇāya | iti |
15.14.218.d: एकशतं बैल्वानि दार्वाचितानि छिन्दत तानि प्रवकलानि कृत्वाचाय चिनुतैकविँशतिं यूपाञ् छिन्दतैकविँशत्य् अरत्नीन् राज्जुदालम् अग्निष्ठं पौतुद्रवाव् उपस्थावानौ षड् बैल्वान् षट् खादिरान् षट् पालाशान् पालाशम् उपशयं पालाशं पात्नीवतं पालाशं विशालयूपम् एकतयानि दारुमयाणि पात्राणि कुरुत षट्त्रिँशतँ स्रुवान् दीर्घदण्डान् षट्त्रिँशतम् अनुवेषान् दीर्घदण्डाँश् चत्वारि वाष्टौ वेन्द्राणसानि चतुश् चक्राणि बृहच्चक्राणि यथा समानि यूपाग्रैः स्युर् अपरिमितान्य् आरोहणमहानसानि कुरुतैकं वैतसं कटं कुरुताश्वस्योपस्तरणाय । इति ।
15.14.218.m: 'Cut one hundred and one [logs] of bilva wood collected as firewood; having cut them into chips and gathered them, stack them; cut twenty-one sacrificial posts (yūpas), twenty-one cubits [in length]: one of rājjudāla wood standing nearest to the fire, two of pūtudru wood standing next to it, six of bilva wood, six of khadira wood, six of palāśa wood, a palāśa post lying alongside, a palāśa post for the Pātnīvata offering, a broad palāśa post; make wooden vessels one by one; thirty-six ladles (sruvas) with long handles, thirty-six stirring sticks (anuveṣas) with long handles; four or eight Indrāṇasa carts with four wheels, with large wheels so that they may be level with the tops of the posts; make unmeasured boarding-carts; make one reed mat to spread under the horse.'

15.14.218.s: athetān rathakṛtaḥ sam̐śāsti svarathaṃ kurutāparimitān rathān kuruta | iti |
15.14.218.d: अथेतान् रथकृतः सँशास्ति स्वरथं कुरुतापरिमितान् रथान् कुरुत । इति ।
15.14.218.m: Then he instructs these chariot-makers: 'Make his own chariot; make unmeasured chariots!'

15.14.219.s: athaitān mayaskṛtaḥ sam̐śāsti | aparimitaṃ carmaṇyaṃ kuruta | iti |
15.14.219.d: अथैतान् मयस्कृतः सँशास्ति । अपरिमितं चर्मण्यं कुरुत । इति ।
15.14.219.m: Then he instructs the leather-workers: 'Make leather gear without measure.'

15.14.219.s: athainān kulālān sam̐śāsti yathaikavim̐śatividhāyāgnaya evam iṣṭakāḥ kuruta tisro mahatīḥ kumbhīḥ kuruta yathāśvaṃ tūparaṃ gomṛgam ity etān sāṅgāñ chrapayeyur aparimitā sthālīḥ kuruta | iti ||
15.14.219.d: अथैनान् कुलालान् सँशास्ति यथैकविँशतिविधायाग्नय एवम् इष्टकाः कुरुत तिस्रो महतीः कुम्भीः कुरुत यथाश्वं तूपरं गोमृगम् इत्य् एतान् साङ्गाञ् छ्रपयेयुर् अपरिमिता स्थालीः कुरुत । इति ॥
15.14.219.m: Then he instructs the potters: 'Make the bricks just as for a twenty-one-fold fire altar. Make three large jars so that they may cook the horse, the hornless goat, and the wild ox with all their limbs. Make pots without measure.'

15.15.219.s: athaitān kālāyasakṛtaḥ sam̐śāsti sāyakaṃ kuruta sittimaṃkalpodakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇatsarum̐ suvarṇam̐ suvarṇatsaruṃ caturaḥ kālāyasān lohāyasatsarūm̐ś caturo lohāyasān kālāyasatsarūn ṣaṭtrim̐śatam̐ suvarṇān rajatatsarūn ṣaṭtrim̐śatam̐ rajatān suvarṇatsarūm̐s trīṇi ca śatāni trayastrim̐śtaṃ ca sauvarṇānām̐ sūcīnāṃ trīṇi ca śatāni trayastrim̐śataṃ ca rājatānāṃ trīṇi ca śatāni trayastrim̐śataṃ ca sīsānām ekaṃ kālāyasasya kamaṇḍaluṃ kurutāśvatejanyai śrapaṇāya | iti |
15.15.219.d: अथैतान् कालायसकृतः सँशास्ति सायकं कुरुत सित्तिमंकल्पोदकं कृष्णं कृष्णत्सरुँ सुवर्णँ सुवर्णत्सरुं चतुरः कालायसान् लोहायसत्सरूँश् चतुरो लोहायसान् कालायसत्सरून् षट्त्रिँशतँ सुवर्णान् रजतत्सरून् षट्त्रिँशतँ रजतान् सुवर्णत्सरूँस् त्रीणि च शतानि त्रयस्त्रिँश्तं च सौवर्णानाँ सूचीनां त्रीणि च शतानि त्रयस्त्रिँशतं च राजतानां त्रीणि च शतानि त्रयस्त्रिँशतं च सीसानाम् एकं कालायसस्य कमण्डलुं कुरुताश्वतेजन्यै श्रपणाय । इति ।
15.15.219.m: Then he instructs the blacksmiths: 'Make an iron arrow, black-pointed, black, with a black handle, a golden [arrow] with a golden handle, four of black iron with copper handles, four of copper with black-iron handles, thirty-six of gold with silver handles, thirty-six of silver with gold handles, three hundred and thirty-three needles of gold, three hundred and thirty-three of silver, three hundred and thirty-three of lead, and make one kamandalu of black iron for cooking the horse-whip.'

15.15.219.s: athaitān suvarṇakṛtaḥ sam̐śāsti paraḥśatam̐ śatapalān niṣkān kuruta suvarṇarajate mahimnoḥ pātre kuruta | ekatayāni sauvarṇāni pātrāṇi kuruta yāvatyaḥ patnayas tāvataḥ sauvarṇān upaśayān kuruta rajatagranthīn rājatān vā suvarṇagranthīn yāvatyaḥ patnayas tāvanti sauvarṇāni kumbakurīrāṇi kuruta rajataśaṅkūni rājatāni vā suvarṇaśaṅkūni yāvatyaḥ patnayas tāvataḥ sauvarṇān kamaṇḍalūn kuruta rajatarāsnān rājatān vā suvarṇarāsnān ekam̐ sauvarṇaṃ vidhavanaṃ kuruta trīṇi sauvarṇāni dhavitrāṇi kuruta rajatadāṇḍāni rājatāni vā suvarṇadaṇḍāni sahasram̐ sauvarṇān kācān kuruta sahasram̐ rājatān sahasram̐ sāmudrān hiraṇmayaṃ kaśipu hiraṇmayaṃ ṣaḍbīśam̐ hiraṇmayam̐ saṃdānam iti ||
15.15.219.d: अथैतान् सुवर्णकृतः सँशास्ति परःशतँ शतपलान् निष्कान् कुरुत सुवर्णरजते महिम्नोः पात्रे कुरुत । एकतयानि सौवर्णानि पात्राणि कुरुत यावत्यः पत्नयस् तावतः सौवर्णान् उपशयान् कुरुत रजतग्रन्थीन् राजतान् वा सुवर्णग्रन्थीन् यावत्यः पत्नयस् तावन्ति सौवर्णानि कुम्बकुरीराणि कुरुत रजतशङ्कूनि राजतानि वा सुवर्णशङ्कूनि यावत्यः पत्नयस् तावतः सौवर्णान् कमण्डलून् कुरुत रजतरास्नान् राजतान् वा सुवर्णरास्नान् एकँ सौवर्णं विधवनं कुरुत त्रीणि सौवर्णानि धवित्राणि कुरुत रजतदाण्डानि राजतानि वा सुवर्णदण्डानि सहस्रँ सौवर्णान् काचान् कुरुत सहस्रँ राजतान् सहस्रँ सामुद्रान् हिरण्मयं कशिपु हिरण्मयं षड्बीशँ हिरण्मयँ संदानम् इति ॥
15.15.219.m: Then he instructs the goldsmiths: 'Make more than a hundred niṣkas weighing a hundred palas. Make the two Mahiman vessels of gold and silver. Make the golden vessels uniform in design. Make as many golden secondary stakes as there are wives, with silver knobs, or silver ones with golden knobs. Make as many golden hair-nets as there are wives, with silver pins, or silver ones with golden pins. Make as many golden kamandalus as there are wives, with silver girdles, or silver ones with golden girdles. Make one golden fanner. Make three golden whisks, with silver handles, or silver ones with golden handles. Make a thousand golden beads, a thousand silver ones, a thousand sea-shell ones; a golden cushion, a golden six-part fetter, and a golden halter.'

15.16.220.s: athaitān nakhakṛtaḥ sam̐śāsti | aparimitāny aṣṭamāni kuruta | iti | athāsyaitāny anyāny upakḷptāni bhavanti śataṃ ghṛtacarmāṇi śataṃ madhucarmāṇi śataṃ taṇḍulacarmāṇi śataṃ pṛthukacarmāṇi śataṃ lājācarmāṇi śataṃ karambhacarmāṇi śataṃ dhānācarmāṇi śatam̐ saktucarmāṇi śataṃ masūsyacarmāṇi śataṃ priyaṅgutaṇḍulacarmāṇīti |
15.16.220.d: अथैतान् नखकृतः सँशास्ति । अपरिमितान्य् अष्टमानि कुरुत । इति । अथास्यैतान्य् अन्यान्य् उपकॢप्तानि भवन्ति शतं घृतचर्माणि शतं मधुचर्माणि शतं तण्डुलचर्माणि शतं पृथुकचर्माणि शतं लाजाचर्माणि शतं करम्भचर्माणि शतं धानाचर्माणि शतँ सक्तुचर्माणि शतं मसूस्यचर्माणि शतं प्रियङ्गुतण्डुलचर्माणीति ।
15.16.220.m: Then he instructs the carpenters: 'Make eighth-parts without measure.' Then these other things are prepared for him: a hundred leather bags of ghee, a hundred leather bags of honey, a hundred leather bags of rice grains, a hundred leather bags of flattened rice, a hundred leather bags of parched grain, a hundred leather bags of groats-porridge, a hundred leather bags of roasted barley, a hundred leather bags of barley meal, a hundred leather bags of lentils, and a hundred leather bags of panic-seed rice grains.

15.16.220.s: athāsyaita ekavim̐śatiḥ pratiprasthātāraḥ sam̐śilṣṭā bhavanty ātmanā dvāvim̐śas
15.16.220.d: अथास्यैत एकविँशतिः प्रतिप्रस्थातारः सँशिल्ष्टा भवन्त्य् आत्मना द्वाविँशस्
15.16.220.m: Then twenty-one pratiprasthātṛ priests are assigned to him, himself being the twenty-second.

15.16.220.s: tejanapadebhyaḥ paśūn samacanti tathārūpāny athārūpām̐s te vidur
15.16.220.d: तेजनपदेभ्यः पशून् समचन्ति तथारूपान्य् अथारूपाँस् ते विदुर्
15.16.220.m: They collect animals from the regions; they know which are suitable and which are not.

15.16.220.s: grāmeṣu grāmyān rakṣanty araṇya āraṇyān giriṣu gaireyān nadīṣu nādeyān pañjareṣu vayām̐si kumbhīṣu sarīsṛpān iti ||
15.16.220.d: ग्रामेषु ग्राम्यान् रक्षन्त्य् अरण्य आरण्यान् गिरिषु गैरेयान् नदीषु नादेयान् पञ्जरेषु वयाँसि कुम्भीषु सरीसृपान् इति ॥
15.16.220.m: In the villages they protect the domestic animals, in the forest the wild animals, on the mountains the mountain-dwelling animals, in the rivers the river animals, in cages the birds, and in jars the reptiles.

15.17.220.s: prasiddhaḥ saṃnivāpas | atha prāyaṇīyena carati prāyaṇīyena caritvā padena carati
15.17.220.d: प्रसिद्धः संनिवापस् । अथ प्रायणीयेन चरति प्रायणीयेन चरित्वा पदेन चरति
15.17.220.m: The gathering of materials is well known. Then he proceeds with the introductory rite. Having proceeded with the introductory rite, he proceeds with the footprint.

15.17.220.s: padena caritvārṣabhe carman sahasreṇa rājānaṃ krītvohyātithyaṃ nirvapati |
15.17.220.d: पदेन चरित्वार्षभे चर्मन् सहस्रेण राजानं क्रीत्वोह्यातिथ्यं निर्वपति ।
15.17.220.m: Having proceeded with the footprint, having bought the King [Soma] on a bull's hide for a thousand [cows], having brought him forward, he pours out the hospitality offering.

15.17.221.m: Having performed the hospitality offering, he then proceeds day after day with the Pravargya and the Upasads.
This indeed lasts twelve days. The twenty-one-fold fire altar is built up.
Its sadas shed has twenty-one roof-mats. Then he carries forward the āhavanīya fire.

15.17.221.s: āhavanīyaṃ praṇīya sadohavirdhāne saṃminoti sadohavirdhāne saṃmityāgnīṣomau praṇayati |
15.17.221.d: आहवनीयं प्रणीय सदोहविर्धाने संमिनोति सदोहविर्धाने संमित्याग्नीषोमौ प्रणयति ।
15.17.221.m: Having carried forward the āhavanīya fire, he erects the sadas and havirdhāna sheds. Having erected the sadas and havirdhāna sheds, he leads forward Agni and Soma.
Having led forward Agni and Soma, he erects the sacrificial post according to the rite of the sacrificial post.

15.17.221.s: svarvantam̐ rājjudālam agniṣṭham utsṛjyāgnīṣomīyaṃ paśum upākaroti
15.17.221.d: स्वर्वन्तँ राज्जुदालम् अग्निष्ठम् उत्सृज्याग्नीषोमीयं पशुम् उपाकरोति
15.17.221.m: Having set aside the cordia post facing the fire, equipped with a top-ring, he dedicates the victim sacred to Agni and Soma.

15.17.221.s: tasya prasiddhaṃ vapayā caritvā vasatīvarīr gṛhṇāti |
15.17.221.d: तस्य प्रसिद्धं वपया चरित्वा वसतीवरीर् गृह्णाति ।
15.17.221.m: Having proceeded with its omentum in the well-known manner, he takes the vasatīvarī waters.

15.17.221.s: atha paśupuroḍāśaṃ nirvapati tam anuvartante 'ṣṭau devasuvām̐ havīm̐ṣi | agnaye gṛhapataye | ity etāni | agnaye gāyatrāya | ity eṣā ca daśahavir iṣṭis
15.17.221.d: अथ पशुपुरोडाशं निर्वपति तम् अनुवर्तन्ते ऽष्टौ देवसुवाँ हवीँषि । अग्नये गृहपतये । इत्य् एतानि । अग्नये गायत्राय । इत्य् एषा च दशहविर् इष्टिस्
15.17.221.m: Then he pours out the animal-cake offering. Following it are the eight oblations of the divine impulsions: those beginning with 'To Agni the house-master', and this is an offering of ten oblations, beginning with 'To Agni related to the Gāyatrī'.

15.17.221.s: tasyā etā yājyāpuro'nuvākyā bhavanti samid diśām āśayā naḥ suvarvid iti |
15.17.221.d: तस्या एता याज्यापुरोऽनुवाक्या भवन्ति समिद् दिशाम् आशया नः सुवर्विद् इति ।
15.17.221.m: Its offering-verses and puronuvākyās are these: 'May the fuel of the directions according to our hope, finding light...'
The animal-cake offerings conclude with the iḍā.

15.17.221.s: patnīsaṃyājāntaḥ paśus | hṛdayaśūlānta ity eke | atha vasatīvarīḥ parihṛtya payām̐si viśiṣyopavasanti |
15.17.221.d: पत्नीसंयाजान्तः पशुस् । हृदयशूलान्त इत्य् एके । अथ वसतीवरीः परिहृत्य पयाँसि विशिष्योपवसन्ति ।
15.17.221.m: The animal sacrifice concludes with the offerings to the wives of the gods; according to some, it concludes with the heart-spit. Then, having carried around the vasatīvarī waters and set aside the milks, they observe the fast.
Then, in the dead of night, they wake up.

15.17.221.s: samānaṃ karmā paridhīnāṃ paridhānāt paridhiṣv anuvartayati kas tvā yunakti sa tvā yunaktu | iti ṣaṇmadhyame ṣaḍ dakṣiṇārdhye pañcottarārdhye |
15.17.221.d: समानं कर्मा परिधीनां परिधानात् परिधिष्व् अनुवर्तयति कस् त्वा युनक्ति स त्वा युनक्तु । इति षण्मध्यमे षड् दक्षिणार्ध्ये पञ्चोत्तरार्ध्ये ।
15.17.221.m: The ritual action is the same up to the laying of the enclosing sticks. He recites over the enclosing sticks the formula: 'Who yokes thee? Let him yoke thee': six over the middle one, six over the southern one, and five over the northern one.
Then, having taken down the King [Soma], he commences the morning litany.

15.17.221.s: parihite prātaranuvāke 'po 'cchaiti | adbhir udaiti | agniṣṭomaṃ kratum upaiti
15.17.221.d: परिहिते प्रातरनुवाके ऽपो ऽच्छैति । अद्भिर् उदैति । अग्निष्टोमं क्रतुम् उपैति
15.17.221.m: When the morning litany is concluded, he goes toward the waters. He comes up with the waters. He approaches the agniṣṭoma rite.

15.17.221.s: prasiddho 'bhiṣavaḥ prasiddhaṃ grahā gṛhyante samānaṃ karmā pavamānāt
15.17.221.d: प्रसिद्धो ऽभिषवः प्रसिद्धं ग्रहा गृह्यन्ते समानं कर्मा पवमानात्
15.17.221.m: The pressing is well known. The soma-cups are drawn in the well-known manner. The ritual action is the same up to the pavamāna chant.

15.17.221.s: pavamānam̐ srapsyan yācati barhiśca śatapalaṃ ca | athāha | udgātar barhiś ca te śatapalaṃ cāśvo ma udgāyatu | iti
15.17.221.d: पवमानँ स्रप्स्यन् याचति बर्हिश्च शतपलं च । अथाह । उद्गातर् बर्हिश् च ते शतपलं चाश्वो म उद्गायतु । इति
15.17.221.m: About to creep toward the pavamāna chant, he asks for sacrificial grass and a hundred-pala [ornament]. Then he says: 'O Udgātṛ, sacrificial grass is for you and a hundred-pala [ornament]; let the horse sing the udgītha for me.'

15.17.222.s: te 'śvasya vāladhim̐ samanvārabhante | agnis te vājin yuṅ | anu tvārabhe svasti mā saṃpāraya vāyus te vājin yuṅ anu tvārabhe svasti mā saṃpāraya | ādityas te vājin yuṅ | anu tvārabhe svasti mā saṃpāraya | iti |
15.17.222.d: ते ऽश्वस्य वालधिँ समन्वारभन्ते । अग्निस् ते वाजिन् युङ् । अनु त्वारभे स्वस्ति मा संपारय वायुस् ते वाजिन् युङ् अनु त्वारभे स्वस्ति मा संपारय । आदित्यस् ते वाजिन् युङ् । अनु त्वारभे स्वस्ति मा संपारय । इति ।
15.17.222.m: They grasp the tail of the horse together, saying: 'Agni is your yoker, O steed; I grasp after you; carry me safely across! Vāyu is your yoker, O steed; I grasp after you; carry me safely across! Āditya is your yoker, O steed; I grasp after you; carry me safely across!'
Then they creep northward toward the pavamāna chant.

15.17.222.s: uttarata eṣa vaḍabāvraja ucchrāyyā pariśrito bhavati taṃ vivrṇvanti |
15.17.222.d: उत्तरत एष वडबाव्रज उच्छ्राय्या परिश्रितो भवति तं विव्र्ण्वन्ति ।
15.17.222.m: To the north, an enclosure of mares has been erected and screened off. They open it.

15.17.222.s: abhy aśvaṃ vaḍabāḥ krandanti | abhy aśvo vaḍabāḥ krandati so 'śvasyodgīthas
15.17.222.d: अभ्य् अश्वं वडबाः क्रन्दन्ति । अभ्य् अश्वो वडबाः क्रन्दति सो ऽश्वस्योद्गीथस्
15.17.222.m: The mares whinny toward the horse. The horse whinnies toward the mares. That is the horse's udgītha.
Then they utter auspicious words together.

15.18.222.s: udagāsīd vā ayam aśvo medhyas | āyur udagāsīt subhūtam udagāsīt | brahmavarcasam udagāsīt | idam udagāsīt | idam udagāsīt | iti puṇyā vācaḥ saṃpravadanti |
15.18.222.d: उदगासीद् वा अयम् अश्वो मेध्यस् । आयुर् उदगासीत् सुभूतम् उदगासीत् । ब्रह्मवर्चसम् उदगासीत् । इदम् उदगासीत् । इदम् उदगासीत् । इति पुण्या वाचः संप्रवदन्ति ।
15.18.222.m: They utter auspicious words together: 'Indeed this sacrificial horse has sung the udgītha!', 'Life has he sung forth!', 'Well-being has he sung forth!', 'Brahminical radiance has he sung forth!', 'This has he sung forth!', 'This has he sung forth!'

15.18.222.s: utsṛjanti vaḍabās | aśvaśālāyām aśvaṃ nigrathnanti | atrāsmā āmukuṣmikam annam upakiranti |
15.18.222.d: उत्सृजन्ति वडबास् । अश्वशालायाम् अश्वं निग्रथ्नन्ति । अत्रास्मा आमुकुष्मिकम् अन्नम् उपकिरन्ति ।
15.18.222.m: They release the mares. They tether the horse in the horse-stall. There they scatter for him food of such and such kind.

15.18.222.s: athāha | udgātar dhenuśataṃ ca te śatapalaṃ ca tvaṃ ma udgāya | iti
15.18.222.d: अथाह । उद्गातर् धेनुशतं च ते शतपलं च त्वं म उद्गाय । इति
15.18.222.m: Then he says: 'O Udgātṛ, a hundred milch cows are for you and a hundred-pala [ornament]; do you sing the udgītha for me!'

15.18.222.s: tasya catasṛṣu bahiṣpavamānas | aṣṭāsv aṣṭāsv ājyāni
15.18.222.d: तस्य चतसृषु बहिष्पवमानस् । अष्टास्व् अष्टास्व् आज्यानि
15.18.222.m: For it, the bahiṣpavamāna chant consists of four verses, the ājyastotras of eight verses each.
The midday pavamāna chant consists of twelve verses, the pṛṣṭhastotras of sixteen verses.
The ārbhava pavamāna chant consists of twenty verses, and the agniṣṭoma saman consists of twenty-four verses.

15.18.222.s: taṃ catuṣṭoma ity ācakṣate samānaṃ karmāśvinād grahāt | āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvaikādaśa raśanā ādāya yūpam abhyaiti
15.18.222.d: तं चतुष्टोम इत्य् आचक्षते समानं कर्माश्विनाद् ग्रहात् । आश्विनं ग्रहं गृहीत्वैकादश रशना आदाय यूपम् अभ्यैति
15.18.222.m: They call that the Catuṣṭoma. The ritual action is the same up to the cup for the Aśvins. Having drawn the cup for the Aśvins and taken eleven halters, he approaches the sacrificial post.

15.18.222.s: svarvantam̐ rājjudālam agniṣṭham utsṛjyaikādaśinān paśūn upākaroti
15.18.222.d: स्वर्वन्तँ राज्जुदालम् अग्निष्ठम् उत्सृज्यैकादशिनान् पशून् उपाकरोति
15.18.222.m: Having raised the central post of rajjudāla wood provided with a chip, he dedicates the animals of the set of eleven.

15.18.223.s: teṣāṃ prasiddhaṃ vapābhiś caritvā prasarpanti prātaḥsavanāya
15.18.223.d: तेषां प्रसिद्धं वपाभिश् चरित्वा प्रसर्पन्ति प्रातःसवनाय
15.18.223.m: Having proceeded with their omenta in the established manner, they proceed forward for the morning pressing.

15.18.223.s: prasarpanti mādhyaṃdināya savanāya prasiddho 'bhiṣavaḥ prasiddhaṃ grahā gṛhyante
15.18.223.d: प्रसर्पन्ति माध्यंदिनाय सवनाय प्रसिद्धो ऽभिषवः प्रसिद्धं ग्रहा गृह्यन्ते
15.18.223.m: They proceed forward for the midday pressing. The extraction is in the established manner. The cups are drawn in the established manner.

15.18.223.s: samānaṃ karmā dākṣiṇebhyas | dākṣiṇāni hutvāṣṭau saṃvargāhutīr juhoti | arvāṅ yajñaḥ saṃkrāmatu | iti
15.18.223.d: समानं कर्मा दाक्षिणेभ्यस् । दाक्षिणानि हुत्वाष्टौ संवर्गाहुतीर् जुहोति । अर्वाङ् यज्ञः संक्रामतु । इति
15.18.223.m: The ritual is the same up to the offerings of the priestly gifts. Having offered the offerings of the priestly gifts, he offers eight samvarga oblations with: "May the sacrifice come hither!"
He gives a third of the priestly gifts.

15.18.223.s: vaiśvakarmaṇāni hutvā nava paryāptīr juhoti bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyat | iti
15.18.223.d: वैश्वकर्मणानि हुत्वा नव पर्याप्तीर् जुहोति भूतं भव्यं भविष्यत् । इति
15.18.223.m: Having offered the vaiśvakarmaṇa oblations, he offers nine paryāpti oblations with: "The past, the present, the future!"

15.18.223.s: nātrāgnyabhiṣekas | ahīnasaṃtatiṃ karoti | ṛjudhā mādhyaṃdinam̐ savanam̐ saṃtiṣṭhate
15.18.223.d: नात्राग्न्यभिषेकस् । अहीनसंततिं करोति । ऋजुधा माध्यंदिनँ सवनँ संतिष्ठते
15.18.223.m: Here there is no sprinkling on the fire. He performs the unbroken continuity of the ahīna rite. The midday pressing is concluded directly.
They proceed forward for the third pressing.

15.18.223.s: prasiddham ādityagraheṇa caritvāgrayaṇaṃ gṛhṇāti samānaṃ karmā pavamānāt
15.18.223.d: प्रसिद्धम् आदित्यग्रहेण चरित्वाग्रयणं गृह्णाति समानं कर्मा पवमानात्
15.18.223.m: Having proceeded with the āditya cup in the established manner, he draws the āgrayaṇa cup. The ritual is the same up to the pavamāna chant.

15.18.223.s: pavamānena caritvā sve dhāman paśubhiś carati teṣāṃ nānā manotā nānā devatā nānā pratyabhimarśanā nānā vasāhomāḥ samāno vanaspatiḥ samānaḥ sviṣṭakṛt praiṣavān samānīḍā samānyo diśas |
15.18.223.d: पवमानेन चरित्वा स्वे धामन् पशुभिश् चरति तेषां नाना मनोता नाना देवता नाना प्रत्यभिमर्शना नाना वसाहोमाः समानो वनस्पतिः समानः स्विष्टकृत् प्रैषवान् समानीडा समान्यो दिशस् ।
15.18.223.m: Having proceeded with the pavamāna chant, he proceeds with the animals at their own station. They have separate manotā hymns, separate deities, separate touchings, [and] separate marrow-oblations; the Vanaspati offering is common, the Sviṣṭakṛt offering with call is common, the iḍā is common, and the directions are common.

15.18.223.s: nānā diśa ity eke samānaṃ karmā patnīsaṃyājebhyas |
15.18.223.d: नाना दिश इत्य् एके समानं कर्मा पत्नीसंयाजेभ्यस् ।
15.18.223.m: "The directions are separate," say some. The ritual is the same up to the patnīsaṃyāja offerings.

15.18.223.d: उपकाश एवैषो ऽग्निष्टोमश् चतुष्टोमः संतिष्ठते पत्नीसंयाजान्तः ॥
15.18.223.m: This agniṣṭoma consisting of four stomas concludes only on the open space, ending with the patnīsaṃyājas.

15.19.223.s: athāsyaitāni śatamaukṣāṇi carmāṇy upastīrṇāni bhavanty uttarām̐ śroṇim uttareṇa pakṣasam̐hitāni |
15.19.223.d: अथास्यैतानि शतमौक्षाणि चर्माण्य् उपस्तीर्णानि भवन्त्य् उत्तराँ श्रोणिम् उत्तरेण पक्षसँहितानि ।
15.19.223.m: Now, these hundred ox-hides of his are spread out, fitted together like wings, to the north of the northern buttock [of the altar].

15.19.223.s: athaiteṣāṃ ghṛtacarmaṇāṃ vim̐śatiṃ vā caturvim̐śatiṃ vāpoddhṛtyāthetarair annāni saṃprayuvanti |
15.19.223.d: अथैतेषां घृतचर्मणां विँशतिं वा चतुर्विँशतिं वापोद्धृत्याथेतरैर् अन्नानि संप्रयुवन्ति ।
15.19.223.m: Then, having taken out twenty or twenty-four of these butter-skins, they mix food-portions with the others.

15.19.223.s: athaiteṣāṃ dārvācitānāṃ vim̐śatiṃ vā caturvim̐śatiṃ vā madhye 'gner acāyaṃ citvāthetarāṇi saṃchidyasaṃchidyaiva saṃprakiranti
15.19.223.d: अथैतेषां दार्वाचितानां विँशतिं वा चतुर्विँशतिं वा मध्ये ऽग्नेर् अचायं चित्वाथेतराणि संछिद्यसंछिद्यैव संप्रकिरन्ति
15.19.223.m: Then, having piled up twenty or twenty-four of these wood-piles in the middle of the fire without gaps, they strew the others, repeatedly cutting them into pieces.

15.19.224.m: He stretches out this four-cornered divine fortress along with the body.

15.19.224.s: api vā pakṣapucchān abhinirūhati yathā samāvatī yūpāgraiḥ syād athainām̐ samucchritya pariśrayanti
15.19.224.d: अपि वा पक्षपुच्छान् अभिनिरूहति यथा समावती यूपाग्रैः स्याद् अथैनाँ समुच्छ्रित्य परिश्रयन्ति
15.19.224.m: Or rather, he pushes out the wings and tail so that it is level with the tops of the sacrificial posts; then, having erected it, they enclose it.

15.19.224.s: tasyodīcīṃ dvāraṃ kurvanti tad etānīndrāṇasāny upavartayanti catvāry anudiśam avāntaradiśāsv itarāṇi yady aṣṭau bhavanti
15.19.224.d: तस्योदीचीं द्वारं कुर्वन्ति तद् एतानीन्द्राणसान्य् उपवर्तयन्ति चत्वार्य् अनुदिशम् अवान्तरदिशास्व् इतराणि यद्य् अष्टौ भवन्ति
15.19.224.m: They make its door facing north. Then they roll up these carts: four according to the cardinal directions, the others in the intermediate directions if there are eight.

15.19.224.s: teṣāṃ catvāraś catvāra ekaikam adhirohanti daśānye rātrikarmiṇas |
15.19.224.d: तेषां चत्वारश् चत्वार एकैकम् अधिरोहन्ति दशान्ये रात्रिकर्मिणस् ।
15.19.224.m: Four [priests] mount each one of them; ten others are night-workers.

15.19.224.s: athaibhya sthālībhir ājyāny abhiharanty aṣṭamair annāni | athādhvaryur ādatte sruvaṃ ca dīrghadaṇḍaṃ darviṃ ca dīrghadaṇḍām
15.19.224.d: अथैभ्य स्थालीभिर् आज्यान्य् अभिहरन्त्य् अष्टमैर् अन्नानि । अथाध्वर्युर् आदत्ते स्रुवं च दीर्घदण्डं दर्विं च दीर्घदण्डाम्
15.19.224.m: Then they bring clarifying butter to them in pots, [and] foods in eighth-measures. Then the adhvaryu priest takes a long-handled dipping-spoon and a long-handled ladle.
The twenty-one pratiprasthātṛ priests take [them], [as do] ten other night-workers.

15.19.224.s: athādhvaryuḥ sruveṇājyasyopahatya trīṇi pūrvāṇi vaiśvadevāni juhoti
15.19.224.d: अथाध्वर्युः स्रुवेणाज्यस्योपहत्य त्रीणि पूर्वाणि वैश्वदेवानि जुहोति
15.19.224.m: Then the adhvaryu priest, taking up ghee with the dipping-spoon, offers the three initial vaiśvadeva oblations.

15.19.224.s: svāhādhim ādhītāya svāhā | iti sruvair evājyānāṃ juhvati datvate svāhā | iti darvair annānām adantakāya svāhā | iti
15.19.224.d: स्वाहाधिम् आधीताय स्वाहा । इति स्रुवैर् एवाज्यानां जुह्वति दत्वते स्वाहा । इति दर्वैर् अन्नानाम् अदन्तकाय स्वाहा । इति
15.19.224.m: With: "Svāhā to reflection, to what has been reflected upon, svāhā!" they offer clarified butter with dipping-spoons alone; with: "To the toothed, svāhā!" food-portions with ladles; [and] with: "To the toothless, svāhā!"

15.19.224.s: ta evam evaitam anuvākam | yadaitasyānuvākasya pāraṃ yanty athaitenānuvākena vyavadadhāti ||
